conditions: A resolution requires a reason and valid current evidence.
exceptions: Implementation or relationship findings require repair or correction; genuine contradictions and missing dependencies remain open.
decisions.reason: Makes warning closure an auditable review disposition rather than an automatic correctness claim.
decisions.text: Active warnings may be explicitly resolved with a reason and current versioned evidence, without a model call. Unknown or repeated warning IDs and invalid or stale citations reject the operation. Resolutions retain their history; changed or unavailable cited sources reactivate a warning. Resolving a warning does not establish decision or relationship quality, change work history, or turn a real implementation or relationship defect into a resolved warning.

decisions.reason: Keeps durable decisions in maintained documentation while preserving tracker discussion as evidence.
decisions.text: Record durable decisions in the appropriate Markdown authority and export changed Hivex knowledge with its sources. Tracker discussion is useful evidence but does not replace maintained project documentation.

exceptions: An unreplayable historical case is not a pass.
decisions.reason: Keeps acceptance grounded in real evaluations and prevents missing evidence from being treated as a semantic result.
decisions.text: Acceptance requires real Luna evaluations and applicable historical gold; simulated protocol tests alone do not suffice. Historical evidence must distinguish missing inputs from semantic disagreement and must not turn an unreplayable case into a pass or an invented owner ruling.

conditions: Cleanup occurs on the first subsequent update, ask, or review.
exceptions: Read-only commands do not perform cleanup.
decisions.reason: Prevents cache reuse across profiles when the old cache keys lack model identity.
decisions.text: Cache identity includes the integration and profile. The first subsequent update, ask, or review clears the old unversioned cache generation because its keys cannot distinguish models; this also removes custom-profile entries from that generation. New versioned entries remain, and read-only commands do not perform this cleanup.

conditions: The check applies before a physical source move or removal of an old procedure.
decisions.reason: Preserves affected-project and reference integrity during source changes.
decisions.text: Before physical source moves or removal of old procedures, check affected projects, links, and identities.

conditions: Contextual prompts and descriptors were bound to the processing contract.
exceptions: Without supporting context, the existing request and global comparison contract remained unchanged.
decisions.reason: Prevented implicit changes to comparison context during update or resume.
decisions.text: In the former contextual-comparison workflow, a context change on the same graph required the current full export, an explicit from/reuse transition, and zero units before execution. Update required a verified managed candidate and matching ingestion store; resume used the frozen context mapping rather than rereading an omitted configuration path or silently reassessing context.

conditions: The syntax gate applies the source-signature limit, including cases Clippy exempts.
exceptions: Clippy exempts trait implementations and non-Rust ABI functions; bodyless foreign declarations and closure captures are excluded from the source limit.
decisions.reason: Provides a consistent explicit-parameter limit while distinguishing external contracts and closure environments.
decisions.text: Functions and methods have at most four explicit parameters, counting the receiver. Clippy covers ordinary functions, inherent methods, and trait declarations; a syntax gate also checks signatures in trait implementations, default methods, and closure inputs. Foreign declarations without a Rust body are external ABI contracts and are excluded; closure captures are environment, not explicit parameters.

conditions: The original comparison and prepared request are complete and revalidated.
exceptions: Comparison feedback alone cannot authorize a candidate change.
decisions.reason: Separates comparison evidence from the independent fidelity basis required for revision.
decisions.text: A standalone fidelity reassessment based on later comparison may supply adverse evidence for revision only after its complete original comparison and prepared request are revalidated. The comparison itself does not authorize a candidate change; the resulting fidelity result must independently meet the sufficient-context and concrete omission-or-distortion criteria.

conditions: Knowledge placement follows whether it is shared or scope-specific.
exceptions: Package- or module-specific knowledge may remain at that level.
decisions.reason: Maintains clear authority and scope while avoiding duplicated rules.
decisions.text: Keep shared decisions at project or monorepo level and package- or module-specific knowledge with its scope; link shared rules instead of duplicating them. Complete project-specific drafts using evidence and owner input, and add documents only for distinct useful purposes.

conditions: Freshness compares declared source and processing inputs.
exceptions: Unrelated code commits do not determine freshness.
decisions.reason: Keeps freshness tied to relevant inputs and protects the accepted graph when admission fails.
decisions.text: Freshness is evaluated against declared source and processing inputs, independently of unrelated code commits. Source or configuration changes remain visible as stale evidence; historical provenance is not rewritten to imply currency. Later admission binds its checks to the exact snapshot and preserves the previously accepted graph on failure.

conditions: Discard follows caller retention or export of completion/admission evidence and is explicit.
exceptions: Read-only retrieval creates no artifacts.
decisions.reason: Preserves execution evidence and makes persistent state changes visible to callers.
decisions.text: Read-only retrieval creates no artifacts; ingestion is explicitly mutating. Retain the store until the caller has exported or retained completion/admission evidence and explicitly discards the cohort. Do not silently rotate stores, delete uncertain attempts, or create a store per invocation. Reject unrelated, unsupported, altered, or oversized stores before sending source text to a model. The CLI exposes progress and reports without requiring inspection of SQLite internals.

conditions: A complete result must fit the caller's budget.
Needed evidence is exported or preserved before explicit retirement.
exceptions: A different graph cannot be used for ordinary resume.
decisions.reason: Makes review lifecycle and cross-snapshot reuse explicit and auditable.
decisions.text: Inspection and complete export are read-only and revalidate assessments, checksums, citations, and coverage. Retire a cohort only explicitly, using its exact plan hash, after preserving needed evidence; retirement rejects unresolved claims and clears retained reviews transactionally. Ordinary resume requires the exact graph. Reuse across snapshots requires the explicit transition operation; source fidelity alone still does not establish cross-source consistency, authority, admission, or implementation grounding.

conditions: Continuation is resumed with its cursor; read bounds can be specified.
decisions.reason: Makes source provenance and incomplete reads visible.
decisions.text: sources returns document metadata and snapshot-bound continuation rather than full text. read returns original text, version, and line ranges with bounded reads and explicit omissions. A working document is not evidence of approval.

exceptions: Registry installation and publication checks belong to release validation, not source build or test prerequisites.
decisions.reason: Separates source development verification from distribution checks.
decisions.text: Package preparation and verification use the Rust development utility and system tar; npm is the distribution channel. Registry installation and publication checks are separate release checks, not prerequisites for building or testing from source.

decisions.reason: This candidate and fidelity process is identified in the supplied guide as retired from the active CLI.
decisions.text: The earlier extraction process used an immutable declared source to produce an unaccepted candidate, retaining literal original-line evidence and preserving conditions, exceptions, and negation.

conditions: This records the earlier implementation baseline only.
exceptions: It is not a current runtime or development-toolchain requirement.
decisions.reason: Preserves the prior language choice as history rather than current policy.
decisions.text: The initial implementation selected TypeScript/Bun, but that runtime choice was later superseded by the approved Rust migration.

conditions: The workflow runs only for owner-triggered published releases or an explicit dispatch for an existing release.
An existing mirror must have identical integrity; mismatched or unauthorized responses fail.
decisions.reason: Ensures the mirror uses the same approved bytes and the intended registry without altering the primary archive.
decisions.text: The GitHub Packages workflow mirrors the stable npm version only for owner-triggered published releases or an explicit dispatch for an existing release. It uses a repository-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN, checks package identity and SHA-512, and publishes the same archive without extracting executable code, rebuilding it, or running installation scripts. An existing mirror must have identical integrity; mismatched or unauthorized registry responses fail. The pinned npm client honors the explicit GitHub registry flag over the archive's default npmjs publish configuration; it does not rewrite the primary archive. Node/npm is only the registry client; Rust owns development, preparation, and verification. npmjs.org remains the normal installation source.

conditions: Existing Git blob limits also apply.
decisions.reason: Makes operation and artifact limits explicit and prevents partial success.
decisions.text: Each operation is bounded to 32 changed text files, 16 contextual code files, 16 sources, 512 claims, 256 selected relationships and a 256 KiB request; retained results must be regular files within 8 MiB. Exceeding a bound fails explicitly rather than returning partial success.

conditions: Applies to the first native package.
exceptions: No other target is authorized by compilation evidence alone.
decisions.reason: Limits initial distribution to the validated platform.
decisions.text: The first native package targets macOS ARM64, the platform validated by the project runner. Keep the selected package identity and command unchanged; compilation evidence alone is insufficient to ship another target.

conditions: Additional targets require runtime-behavior and package testing before addition.
decisions.reason: Constrains the release target to the tested native package.
decisions.text: Prepare releases from a reviewed Git revision on the admitted macOS ARM64 runner. The npm package declares Darwin and ARM64; do not add another target until both its runtime behavior and package have been tested.

conditions: The cohort must be complete and verified.
exceptions: Neither successful extraction nor assembly alone establishes currentness or admission.
decisions.reason: Defines the graph projection and preserves provenance without inferring precedence from model output.
decisions.text: A graph snapshot is built from a complete verified ingestion cohort and keeps source declarations, claims, relations, and extraction evidence distinct. Claims and edges use content-derived identities, not serialization order or model-local IDs for precedence. Preserve literal citations and their original source revision. Extraction success and assembly do not establish currentness or admission.

conditions: The pair included both complete sources, candidate statements, and source-local relationships.
exceptions: A source could not occupy both sides, and a source without claims could not form a valid pair.
decisions.reason: Defined bounded, complete inputs for the earlier pair-comparison workflow.
decisions.text: The former comparison operation assessed a selected pair of distinct, complete, versioned sources, each with extracted claims, using the admitted native route. Missing or oversized input failed before invocation rather than becoming empty or truncated. Preparation showed the complete bounded request without a model call; execution produced one result and no per-comparison files.

conditions: The stated shipped integration is current setup, not a permanent support commitment.
exceptions: The implementing agent may use another model.
decisions.reason: Distinguishes Hivex’s selected knowledge profile from the implementing agent’s model.
decisions.text: The default knowledge profile is gpt-6-luna at max effort, while model profile and execution integration remain separate choices. Codex is the only integration currently shipped; the implementing agent may use another model, and there is no silent fallback.

conditions: Retain the artifact until publication and any required verification are complete.
decisions.reason: Preserves artifact identity and directs release cleanup to the tracker procedure.
decisions.text: Record the published version, exact artifact hash, and registry result. Do not rebuild or repack between approval and publication, and retain the artifact until publication and any required verification finish. Git integration and completed branch cleanup follow the tracker procedure.

conditions: The result must come from the actual quality job and its intended runner.
exceptions: If CI is unavailable, retain applicable local verification.
decisions.reason: Makes completion and execution environment part of the verification evidence.
decisions.text: Treat verification as passing only after the actual job confirms its runner image and architecture and completes formatting, compilation, Clippy with warnings denied, unit tests, package preparation, CLI contracts against the release executable, and exact-archive verification. Queued, skipped, or interrupted runs are not passes; if CI is unavailable, retain applicable local verification.

conditions: The cost distinction depends on whether the repository is public or private.
decisions.reason: Describes the current public/private runner cost boundary without implying the workflow changes account capacity.
decisions.text: Standard GitHub-hosted runners are free for public repositories. While the repository is private, jobs use the account's included minutes and applicable billing. This workflow does not change account budgets or purchase capacity.

conditions: Reuse specifies both the destination revision and a zero model budget.
decisions.reason: Makes snapshot transitions explicit and reviewable before further extraction.
decisions.text: `ingest --export` produces a read-only complete export of the frozen plan, all source rows, and their results or checkpoints. Reuse is explicit: `ingest --reuse <export> --ref <new-commit> --max-units 0` creates a reviewable checkpoint before new extraction.

conditions: The harness remains responsible for discovering findings, testing and accepting the change.
Keep the claim scope explicit; a contradicted allegation may correctly dismiss a finding.
exceptions: Every result keeps accepted and implementationAccepted false.
decisions.reason: Provides scoped evidence about a claim without making a project-wide acceptance decision.
decisions.text: Ground a specific review claim against the committed implementation and a fresh admitted manifest. Report whether that claim is supported, contradicted or unresolved, without approving the whole implementation.

conditions: TDD is optional only for sufficiently defined critical flows.
The default independent reviewer matches the implementation agent's model and effort.
decisions.reason: Provides task-oriented practice without mandating a compulsory skill sequence.
decisions.text: Practice guidance favors domain-driven design, meaningful responsibilities, risk- and value-based testing, and one independent review by default. TDD is optional for sufficiently defined critical flows; the reviewer matches the implementation agent's model and effort. Use local knowledge before model-assisted interpretation and explain technical details when they matter to the owner's understanding or decisions.

conditions: The caller may supply additional source IDs, explicit versioned code context or a revised review scope when context is insufficient.
exceptions: No implicit model retry or automatic context truncation is allowed.
decisions.reason: Preserves relationship context while making selection limits and gaps visible.
decisions.text: Select up to eight lexical claim matches and optional explicit source IDs, then expand the complete source neighborhood along supersedes, exception-to and requires relationships in both directions. Provide full selected Markdown, declarations, claims and relationships, and disclose unexpanded relationships and non-exhaustive selection. Lexical matches do not establish semantic completeness; when omitted material is needed, report insufficient context rather than retrying implicitly, truncating context or claiming global consistency.

conditions: Cache reuse requires an identical request context, schema, and model profile.
decisions.reason: Supports resumable work without giving caches documentary authority.
decisions.text: Extraction and checking are checkpointed. Successful structured results are cached by the complete request, schema, and model profile; identical requests can be reused without a call, while changed context invalidates the cache entry. Relationship discovery is bounded rather than exhaustive, and cache contents are an optimization, not authority.

conditions: Bun 1.4.2 was the supported minimum and reproducible development/CI baseline.
exceptions: Compatible newer runtimes were accepted; routine tool updates were not to be rejected solely because their version number differed.
decisions.reason: The ADR explicitly marks its runtime and development requirements as superseded by the Rust migration.
decisions.text: The superseded Bun setup used bun install with a committed lockfile for development and bun ci for frozen installs. Bun 1.4.2 was the minimum and pinned development/CI baseline, while compatible newer versions were accepted. It also specified Bun’s isolated layout, a seven-day minimum release age, an initially empty trusted-dependency allowlist, and review of lifecycle-script additions.

exceptions: Hexagonal layers and a second orchestration runtime are not required.
decisions.reason: Makes domain boundaries meaningful without multiplying products or imposing architecture layers.
decisions.text: Organize Hivex as a modular monolith around its language and invariants. A domain boundary requires meaningful capability behavior and a small interface; directory names alone do not establish one. Keep one product without mandatory hexagonal layers or a second orchestration runtime.

decisions.reason: Records the stated development workflow.
decisions.text: Development is issue-first and uses coherent pull requests, independent review covering scope, correctness, and standards, and CI on the final commit.

conditions: The destination binding must match the complete old archive for a repeated transition.
exceptions: An altered archive is rejected even if the destination plan is already present.
decisions.reason: Prevents partial replacement and binds repeated transitions to the reviewed source archive.
decisions.text: Before reuse, validate the archive against the complete current store, including row state, results, attempts, revision history, checkpoints, and usage. Running rows, active checkpoints, and uncertain invocations block replacement. Transition is immediate and atomic: validation or capacity failure leaves the old cohort unchanged. Repetition on an initialized destination is accepted only for the same complete old archive recorded by its transition binding.

conditions: A historical snapshot may be inspected against its original revision.
exceptions: Unrelated code changes alone do not make the documentation graph stale.
decisions.reason: Prevents flags or checksums from substituting for integrity, evidence and revision checks.
decisions.text: Every read revalidates integrity, source evidence and embedded semantic assessments. Evaluate freshness against the requested project revision; changed documentary or processing inputs prevent a historical snapshot from serving as current acceptance evidence.

conditions: An agent may proceed with integration only when the owner explicitly approves that specific PR.
exceptions: An invalid review may be rerun.
decisions.reason: Protects tracked scope, shared branch integrity, and owner control of integration.
decisions.text: Use an existing issue for an already tracked requirement; branch from current remote main, keep each PR to one coherent change, and preserve commit history when merging. Do not push directly to main or force-push a shared branch. Apply review findings before acceptance: an invalid review may be rerun, but an adverse finding must be resolved on its merits. The owner decides whether each PR is merged. Agents stop before integration unless that specific PR has explicit owner approval; a general implementation approval does not authorize merging.

conditions: This describes the current quality workflow.
decisions.reason: Records the approved runner change without making the current setup a permanent requirement.
decisions.text: The quality workflow currently runs on an ephemeral GitHub-hosted macOS ARM64 runner, replacing the personal Mac runner with owner approval; the document path remains for package and historical links.

conditions: Answer reuse requires unchanged supplied context.
decisions.reason: Defines bounded, resumable consultation behavior and visible partial coverage.
decisions.text: An ask detects source changes, updates at most one bounded batch prioritizing matching fragments, relevant documents, and known dependencies, then answers over available decisions and original Markdown. Its default budget is three calls for the complete update, check, and answer operation. Resuming the same task with an authorized higher total retains progress and consumption; unchanged tasks reuse their answer, and remaining coverage stays visible for explicit updates.

conditions: Consolidate assertions or fixtures only when another test retains the same guarantee.
exceptions: CLI checks are used where process, filesystem, or public-output behavior matters.
decisions.reason: Maintains meaningful guarantees while avoiding redundant tests and arbitrary counts.
decisions.text: Tests should protect observable rules and meaningful boundaries with focused unit tests for invariants, integration contract tests for execution, and CLI checks where process, filesystem, or public-output behavior matters. Consolidate repeated assertions and fixtures only when another test retains the same guarantee; do not remove coverage to make a refactor pass or pursue an arbitrary test count. Keep audit evidence with its tracked work; permanent documentation records the policy rather than duplicating a code-test catalogue.

conditions: The zombie-state qualification applies to Linux orphan processes.
exceptions: Cleanup does not claim that Hivex has reaped orphan PID entries.
decisions.reason: States what process cleanup can and cannot establish.
decisions.text: On Linux, cleanup confirms termination of the owned process group and reaps the directly spawned server. A bounded process-state check may confirm remaining members are terminated (Z or X); live, unknown, or unreadable state does not confirm cleanup.

conditions: The hosted workflow must pass first.
exceptions: The change does not include runners belonging to other repositories.
decisions.reason: Scopes cleanup to Hivex and makes hosted verification its prerequisite.
decisions.text: Retire the personal runner only after the hosted workflow passes. Stop and uninstall Hivex's local runner service, remove its repository registration, and verify no Hivex self-hosted runner remains; leave other repositories' runners alone.

conditions: Applies when a project has multiple bounded contexts.
exceptions: A monorepo need not duplicate one shared product glossary.
decisions.reason: Accommodates context-specific language while preserving shared knowledge.
decisions.text: Multiple bounded contexts may keep their own glossaries and decisions, linked by a small context map; a monorepo need not duplicate a shared product glossary.

decisions.reason: Keeps derived knowledge subordinate to project documentation and agent responsibility.
decisions.text: Hivex provides reusable project knowledge and retrieval across project-specific Markdown. Markdown remains authoritative, and the responsible agent directs the work.

decisions.reason: Defines initialization’s side effects and repeat behavior.
decisions.text: Initialization creates missing foundation documents, skill links, source configuration, and Git ignore rules; reports created, preserved, and updated paths; makes no model calls; and does not install dependencies, configure global tools, or write to GitHub. Repeating it preserves existing Markdown, configuration, graph, and history.

conditions: Recovery applies to the same selected pair and unchanged neighbor settings.
exceptions: Completed adverse comparisons are not retry candidates.
decisions.reason: Preserves invocation history and limits recovery to explicitly eligible failures.
decisions.text: Pair comparisons support the shared explicit safe-recovery contract. Recovery uses the selected pair ID and unchanged neighbor settings; only eligible invocation failures may be retried, while completed adverse comparisons remain blockers. Earlier receipts, unknown consumption, and the three-attempt total limit persist across compatible graph reuse.

conditions: Expected outcomes and cost are explicit for the cases.
decisions.reason: Validates the public workflow, interpretation, and portability rather than incidental internals.
decisions.text: Validation uses bounded real cases for conflict, valid exception, indirect dependency, insufficient evidence, and document change, with explicit expected outcomes and measured cost. It also exercises a differently organized Markdown project and an agent using the skill; tests target the public CLI and native protocol seam rather than incidental representations.

conditions: The migration preserves the useful contracts of the earlier test suite.
exceptions: The optional TypeScript Markdown template is retained because it is not executable development tooling.
decisions.reason: Defines complete development-toolchain migration while preserving compatibility evidence.
decisions.text: Complete Rust migration removes TypeScript, JavaScript, and Bun from Hivex development. Cargo/Rust handles tests, synthetic protocol execution, archive preparation, and artifact verification. Preserve useful CLI, storage, accounting, failure, and recovery contracts rather than treating test counts or language statistics as acceptance criteria. Retire replaced source, lockfile, and configuration; retain fixed SQL compatibility data and Git history. The optional TypeScript Markdown template remains package content, not development tooling.

decisions.reason: Defines the scope of work accounting and historical-knowledge recovery.
decisions.text: Work comprises one requested update, consultation, or review, including its phases and resumptions. Its budget applies across phases and resumed attempts; resumption does not reset usage, and unknown consumption remains visible. Recovery incorporates useful historical decisions, reasons, and lessons into their appropriate authorities while identifying obsolete, duplicate, or merely operational material.

conditions: When a project is rolling out the shared snapshot.
decisions.reason: Distinguishes creating an artifact from completing the project's adoption workflow.
decisions.text: Saving a snapshot alone does not complete a project's rollout; publication and process retirement follow the project's normal workflow.

conditions: Historical sources require focused selection or a known dependency for consultation.
decisions.reason: Makes omitted source text discoverable without treating archive availability or links as consultation.
decisions.text: Search covers extracted decisions and original Markdown. Historical sources are not searched into an ordinary consultation merely because they are available; select a focused source or use a known dependency. Name necessary historical evidence that is excluded or unavailable. Unconsulted historical or unavailable local links require responsible-agent assessment through reading or source selection; a link alone does not ingest an archive.

conditions: Numeric ADR prefixes apply where the project uses that convention.
exceptions: Keep conventional entrypoints and names required by project tools or languages.
decisions.reason: Supports consistent naming without breaking established entrypoints or references.
decisions.text: Prefer kebab-case for authored document and directory names, and numeric ADR prefixes where that convention is used. Preserve conventional entrypoint names and tool-required names; preserve links and history when renaming.

conditions: A converted quote wrap must map to source text, never code; inline spacing is preserved.
exceptions: Code citations always use literal matching.
decisions.reason: Allows limited paragraph-wrap differences without weakening source-byte or code-citation integrity.
decisions.text: Documentary citation checking first tries a literal match; a conservative Markdown fallback may join soft wraps and continuation indentation only within one parsed paragraph, including a single list item, while respecting original section scope and paragraph boundaries. Code citations remain literal; code, HTML, tables, frontmatter, hard breaks and Markdown structural tokens stay strict. The check does not rewrite source or quotes, change hashes or receipts, or promote a failed result.

conditions: A replacement must demonstrate the capabilities it is intended to replace before the accepted graph is displaced.
decisions.reason: Protects accepted knowledge during replacement work.
decisions.text: Keep the accepted Opus graph intact until a replacement demonstrates the capabilities it is intended to replace.

conditions: Migration occurs only as part of a valid retry or transition and cannot cross an active claim or invocation.
exceptions: Prior failed receipts are retained as diagnostic history, not additional semantic evidence for admission.
decisions.reason: Preserves retry and transition history without confusing past failures with current assessments.
decisions.text: Format 3 retains up to two complete previous failed results separately from the latest result, within the per-result, combined-history, and store limits. Migration from formats 1 or 2 is atomic with the first valid retry, requires no active claim, and preserves the transition binding and other rows; supported formats remain readable without migration. Format 4 binds transitions to the exact predecessor plan and upgrades formats 1–3 transactionally without crossing an active invocation. Exports expose prior attempts and count each receipt once, preserving unmeasured usage; compatible transitions carry history and budgets, while removed or incompatible units retain history in the archive. Admission uses successful current assessments only; earlier failures are diagnostic history, which retirement clears.

conditions: For the replacement workflow, consultation, and source-based repair.
exceptions: Partial knowledge remains usable within its limits.
decisions.reason: Preserves bounded, resumable work and source authority while avoiding unnecessary protocol.
decisions.text: The replacement workflow processes bounded document batches with one additional knowledge check, keeps partial knowledge usable, and preserves work budgets across phases and resumption. Before answering, a consultation processes at most one bounded pending batch; remaining corpus coverage stays explicit. Source-based repair replaces interpretations without changing doctrine; check warnings remain scoped, and public evidence is limited to source coordinates, version, and text. Avoid a new abstraction or protocol without a concrete requirement.

conditions: For an existing project, the adopting agent incorporates the policy into the appropriate authority.
exceptions: Installing an updated package does not retroactively rewrite project policy.
decisions.reason: Keeps the policy authoritative in project Markdown and avoids confusing it with review or merge authorization.
decisions.text: The reusable knowledge-before-merge policy belongs in the engineering foundation and is routed to by the tracker procedure. New projects receive it through `init`; an adopting agent must incorporate it into the appropriate authority of an existing project while preserving explicit owner decisions. Installing an updated package does not rewrite existing project policy. The gate supplements, rather than replaces, implementation review, behavioral verification, and merge-authorization policy.

conditions: Changed code, documentation, graph or processing contract requires a corresponding new assessment.
Preserve original hashes and receipts for the identified prior prompt variants, which retain the same validator and response schema; arbitrary historical contracts are not admitted.
exceptions: A checksum binds integrity but does not prove authorship.
decisions.reason: Maintains provenance and enables revalidation without repeating model work.
decisions.text: Use the admitted native Luna/max route and retain positive, negative and unresolved assessments with invocation evidence, usage and unmeasured failures. Rejected responses remain hashed untrusted diagnostics, not assessments, and are not implicitly retried. Bind results to graph, code, sources, relationships, selection, prompt/schema/policy, assessment and invocation identities; the invocation hash includes the full original receipt before normalization. A caller-owned stdout artifact is deterministically rechecked against the current checkout without a model call.

conditions: When updating the toolchain or addressing new diagnostics.
exceptions: Individual lint decisions remain explicit; the full restriction and nursery groups are not enabled.
decisions.reason: Maintains strict but considered linting instead of suppressing diagnostics mechanically.
decisions.text: Enable Clippy `all` and `pedantic` at lower group priority and deny warnings in CI. Retain pedantic defaults and avoid suppressions or exclusions introduced for this adoption. Explicitly name `dbg_macro`, `todo`, `unimplemented`, and `redundant_else`; do not enable the full `restriction` or `nursery` groups. Assess new diagnostics by meaning rather than allowing or raising thresholds just to pass.

conditions: Admission was against current HEAD; against was for historical inspection.
exceptions: A single claim-bearing source required source fidelity but no cross-source comparison.
decisions.reason: Records the former graph-admission criteria without making them current requirements for the replacement workflow.
decisions.text: The former admission contract required an exact fresh candidate graph and complete successful source-fidelity and comparison cohorts under the recorded contract, covering every source and selected pair once. Pending, interrupted, negative, malformed, stale, or oversized evidence was inadmissible; unresolved contradictions and precedence cycles blocked automatic admission. An empty graph was not admissible.

decisions.reason: Separates source freshness from interpretation quality and keeps Markdown authoritative.
decisions.text: Snapshot responses identify current, stale, and unavailable source versions, pending units, and warnings. Changed or absent sources are not silently current, while matching sources remain reusable. Freshness does not establish that an interpretation is correct; cited Markdown remains authoritative.

conditions: Compatibility is determined against the complete processing contract and source unit.
exceptions: Changed or new units are pending; failed results are not automatically retried.
decisions.reason: Preserves provenance and accounting when compatible work is reused across snapshots.
decisions.text: Reuse compares the full processing contract and source unit, including identifier, path, collection, content hash, section, authority, prompt hash, and limits. Changed or new units become pending. Compatible candidates and safely retained failures carry their attempts, revision history, usage, and budgets unchanged, without automatic retry. The new result binds to the current plan and snapshot and the original result hash, rather than copying the old plan or rewriting the original receipt. Store reads and graph assembly revalidate the unit-contract association; graph receipt hashes cover the full current record. Later revision starts a new extraction origin while retaining the reused candidate's history and remaining budgets.

conditions: Sources, graph, and execution profile must still match to resume the check.
Any new invocation remains subject to the original work budget.
exceptions: The selected model may not accept the packet size.
decisions.reason: Separates context capacity from work accounting and prevents reuse of stale checks.
decisions.text: The consultation context limit defaults to 65,536 bytes and accepts explicit limits from 1,024 to 1,073,741,824 bytes. If a materialized check pauses for context, resume the same task with a sufficient limit only while its sources, graph, and execution profile still match. Hivex retains the extraction and runs the pending check; more context does not increase the work budget, permit repeating an adverse check, or guarantee model acceptance.

decisions.reason: Keeps admission evidence complete and preserves the scope of amendments and relationships.
decisions.text: The admitted snapshot retains the candidate, source assessments, deterministic comparison selection, comparisons and derived relationships. Preserve all claims even when a scoped amendment applies; retain relationship conditions, exceptions, affected scope and evidence from both endpoints. A content hash binds the complete snapshot as its manifest identity.

conditions: The requested configuration and effective profile must be compatible.
exceptions: Incompatible protocol or profile stops execution instead of triggering fallback.
decisions.reason: Makes invocation and compatibility checks explicit and capability-based.
decisions.text: Using the default knowledge profile requires an authenticated Codex CLI session with Luna/max available. Explicit model and effort selections must be advertised by the runtime, and both requested configuration and effective profile are validated. Codex compatibility is based on app-server protocol and effective account, model, and isolation settings rather than an exact CLI version; an admitted invocation records its CLI version.

conditions: When loading a shared snapshot into a project with local work state.
decisions.reason: Keeps portable knowledge separate from local execution state and protects in-progress work.
decisions.text: `.hivex/knowledge.sqlite` is the local working store for queries, incremental work, attempts, budgets, and caches; `.hivex/knowledge.lock` remains local. The shared snapshot excludes process identities, locks, pending invocations, and the model-response cache. Loading a snapshot must not overwrite unfinished work, erase failed attempts, or reset an existing budget.

decisions.reason: Distinguishes source, processing fragments, historical records, and version selections.
decisions.text: A document is a selected Markdown file wherever the project keeps it. An archive preserves replaced decisions and reasons as historical evidence, not presumed current authority. An ingestion unit is a bounded source fragment with original coordinates, not a separate authority. A document version identifies exact contents, including an uncommitted working copy, without implying approval; a snapshot groups selected versions for a particular work item.

conditions: Context mappings must use valid, distinct primary/supporting sources and contain no unused configured pairs.
exceptions: Supporting sources can inform precedence but cannot become claim targets or relationship endpoints.
decisions.reason: Allows bounded documentary context without changing the selected primary pair.
decisions.text: Supporting context is limited to two existing sources from the same verified graph and snapshot. A versioned JSON mapping contains source IDs only and is limited to 128 KiB; supporting Markdown is supplied with authority and original positions but without extracted claims. Primary sources alone remain relationship endpoints. Supporting evidence may justify scoped precedence, but does not itself create an exception or resolve doctrine; relationships still require evidence from both primary endpoints.

decisions.reason: Keeps documentary authority distinct from its derived index.
decisions.text: Markdown is the source of project knowledge; the derived graph helps locate and interpret it but is not itself authoritative.

conditions: Inspection and scanning apply to the exact archive intended for release.
decisions.reason: Requires artifact-specific content review and traceable inspection.
decisions.text: Inspect the exact archive for required public contents and excluded private or development material. Scan extracted contents for secrets and unintended private material, recording the checks and archive hash. Any changed archive requires a fresh inspection.

conditions: Validation in two consuming projects preceded owner approval.
exceptions: The runtime changed; the product contract and cohesive domain modules were retained.
decisions.reason: Records the approved runtime replacement and its completed integration.
decisions.text: After adoption was validated in two consuming projects, the owner approved replacing the TypeScript/Bun runtime with Rust while retaining the product contract and cohesive domain modules. The complete Rust CLI was verified and integrated; the earlier TypeScript CLI served as the compatibility reference during migration.

conditions: Verification applies to the exact archive intended for release.
exceptions: Model scenarios use only the Rust synthetic app-server.
decisions.reason: Requires artifact-level native verification beyond a source build.
decisions.text: Run the verifier against that exact archive. It checks integrity and the public allowlist, rejects unsafe paths and links, and exercises the native executable in a clean temporary project and environment without Bun or Node.js. Fixtures check executable mode, JSON behavior, and preservation of retained state; model scenarios run only through the Rust synthetic app-server. CI also tests the release executable. A successful source build alone is insufficient.

conditions: Current supplied Markdown and current replacement endpoints are required to assess relationship removal or replacement.
Unjustified loss preserves the prior graph and attempted result.
exceptions: Inherited uncertainty alone is not a new rejection finding.
decisions.reason: Prevents materializing a candidate from silently discarding supported knowledge or treating inherited uncertainty as a current defect.
decisions.text: Admission checks evaluate materialized decisions and relationships, including local validation discards. If a candidate would lose relationships whose source authorities remain available, the check must justify the loss or identify supported replacements; otherwise the prior graph remains available and the work fails with RELATIONSHIP_LOSS. Current findings affecting a replacement or its endpoints block admission, while inherited uncertainty alone does not veto an explicitly justified replacement.

conditions: Archived sources are brought in only through focused selection or a known dependency.
decisions.reason: Applies archive selection and corpus prioritization to resumable work.
decisions.text: Archived sources are outside ordinary updates. A focused ask or review adds only selected bounded units to resumable work; known dependencies may add needed ranges. Work budget, graph knowledge, and cache survive resumption. An unrelated historical-document change does not reset a consultation budget. At the loaded-corpus limit, current documents take priority; narrow configured scope to access sources outside reported coverage.

conditions: This compatibility check is required before registry publication.
exceptions: Node.js is used for this release-only registry-client check, not source development, tests, or artifact preparation.
decisions.reason: Adds an installation-level compatibility check without making Node.js a development requirement.
decisions.text: Before registry publication, install the exact archive into a clean temporary prefix using npm with scripts, audit, and funding disabled, then verify the installed command and metadata. This release-only compatibility check uses the registry client's Node.js installation; source development, tests, and artifact preparation do not require Node.js.

conditions: Unresolved claimants or missing or altered archive results blocked replacement.
Retirement required the exact plan hash and preservation of needed evidence.
exceptions: A known preflight admission failure before any accepted turn, with confirmed cleanup or no observed server, remained a retained failure rather than an uncertain invocation. Unconfirmed starts or interruptions, missing acceptance evidence, and failed cleanup blocked replacement.
decisions.reason: Made replacement explicit and atomic while retaining prior evidence and distinguishing known preflight failures from uncertain execution.
decisions.text: The former review-cohort transition required preserving the candidate graph and complete export, validating the archive against the old plan and retained rows, and replacing the cohort transactionally in the same store. Compatible reviews could be reused; changed or new sources remained pending and removed sources stayed in the caller's archive. Repeating the current transition preserved progress; ordinary execution handled pending sources within budget, and retained negative results continued to block admission.

conditions: Applies to direct dependencies between domains.
exceptions: A domain's own modules and the shared `error` and `compatibility` utilities are permitted; the CLI and binary entry point compose domains.
decisions.reason: Makes the allowed domain dependency graph explicit.
decisions.text: Direct dependencies beyond a domain's own modules and the shared `error` and `compatibility` utilities are limited as follows: documents and foundation have none; knowledge may use documents, work, and execution; work may use documents, knowledge, and execution; execution may use documents, knowledge, and work; integrations may use execution; consultation may use documents, knowledge, work, execution, and review; review may use documents, knowledge, work, and execution. The CLI and binary entry point compose the domains.

conditions: This Clippy setting supplements the separate function-local nesting rule.
exceptions: Its five-level total includes containers and is not equivalent to three body nesting levels.
decisions.reason: Retains a useful supplementary lint without confusing its counting model with the project rule.
decisions.text: Use Clippy's `excessive_nesting` threshold of five total syntactic levels as a supplementary check, not as the definition of the three nested body levels. It counts enclosing function, `impl`, trait, and inline-module blocks; out-of-line modules reset its count. Deep inline containers may therefore make it stricter, but methods should not be moved solely to evade that count.

conditions: Retirement of old active machinery follows verification of the replacement.
exceptions: Early use may precede complete legacy recovery; the archive need not recreate a fleet of old machinery.
decisions.reason: Distinguishes early utility from verified closure while preserving useful historical evidence.
decisions.text: Early use may precede complete legacy recovery. Full closure also requires recovering useful historical knowledge and retiring old active machinery after the replacement is verified. Preserve Git history and necessary external evidence; a legacy evidence document can suffice, and a successful package build alone does not establish full workflow validation.

conditions: Fresh fidelity review is required before admitting a successful replacement.
exceptions: Ingestion revision does not update the currentness of existing assessments.
decisions.reason: Prevents revision from being mistaken for review or admission of a replacement candidate.
decisions.text: A successful replacement remains a candidate and requires fresh fidelity review before admission. Unrelated source candidates remain intact. Reassociating compatible source reviews uses the separate source-review operation; ingestion revision does not relabel assessments as current.

conditions: Capacity is reserved before work begins.
Storage is local, not on a network filesystem.
exceptions: Experimental version-1 stores are rejected intact before mutation or model invocation.
decisions.reason: Bounds persistent work state and prevents unsafe migration or capacity-driven partial work.
decisions.text: Use one local, Git-excluded SQLite store, normally `.hivex/ingestion.sqlite`, for a single cohort and bounded reports and unaccepted candidates. Limits are 2,048 sources, an 8 MiB plan, an 8 MiB result per source, and a 128 MiB database. The format history begins with version 2 and its cohort checksum; version 3 adds bounded semantic revision history, and version 4 adds an explicit-reuse binding. Valid earlier cohorts are read intact and upgraded only after a successful mutation or transition. Reserve capacity before work and fail explicitly if it is exhausted. Use local rather than network storage; the rollback journal is recovered or removed with normal transaction handling.

decisions.reason: Requires reviewable evidence and distinguishes completed checks from pending or skipped checks.
decisions.text: Complete relevant verification and independent review before opening a clear PR linked to its issue. Explain behavior, validation actually completed, and material limits. Follow CI to an actual result; queued or skipped checks are not passes.

conditions: Diagnostics are validated for size and hash when read.
exceptions: Older receipts may omit the diagnostics field; over-limit text is omitted with metadata retained.
decisions.reason: Preserves bounded evidence of rejected extraction output without changing extraction behavior.
decisions.text: For invalid extraction, retain rejected text in its existing attempt up to 32 KiB of UTF-8, with its SHA-256 and byte count; above the cap, retain the metadata and mark the text omitted for the limit. These untrusted diagnostics persist through checkpoints, safe retries, export, and reuse. Readers validate their size and hash and reject diagnostics attached to a successful attempt; older receipts may omit the field. At twelve attempts the text cap totals 384 KiB, within the store limits, and retention does not change prompts, retry policy, storage limits, or invocation accounting.

conditions: Publication requires the approval applicable to the exact artifact.
decisions.reason: Separates reproducible artifact verification from registry release authorization.
decisions.text: Keep npm as the distribution channel and package.json as metadata. Cargo builds the admitted native target; a Rust utility stages the public allowlist and invokes system tar, then verification extracts the archive and exercises its executable without Bun or Node on PATH. Installation and publication are separate registry compatibility and release steps; toolchain changes do not authorize republishing or publishing an artifact.

conditions: Reject empty changesets, binary or invalid UTF-8 content, symlink/submodule changes, and requests outside declared bounds.
exceptions: Historical code inspection is not current implementation acceptance.
decisions.reason: Binds review evidence to a complete, stable implementation change rather than unbound snippets.
decisions.text: Use a clean checkout, current HEAD and an explicit base revision. Derive the comparison from the base revision's merge base, record both resolved commits and a digest of the complete changed-file manifest, and supply complete before/after versions with object IDs, paths and modes. Reject unsupported or oversized changes; a checkout changed during execution cannot yield current review evidence.

conditions: Integration may proceed only with explicit owner approval for the specific PR.
decisions.reason: Keeps per-PR integration authority with the owner.
decisions.text: The owner makes the final merge decision for each PR. Agents prepare reviewed, passing PRs and stop before integration unless the owner explicitly approves that specific PR. A general implementation GO, readiness label, or access to the owner's credentials is not that approval.

decisions.reason: Reflects the Rust migration and the explicit retirement of the prior Bun development setup.
decisions.text: Use Cargo with the committed lockfile for runtime, development tools, and tests. The development gate uses the stable configured toolchain, two-space formatting, Clippy all and pedantic checks with warnings denied, source-quality and domain-dependency gates, and behavioral checks, with scope defined by the Rust quality standard. TypeScript, JavaScript, and Bun are retired from Hivex development; the earlier Bun installation decision is historical.

conditions: All supplied claims and relationships must be assessed.
exceptions: An empty extraction is eligible for a successful review only with explicit, evidenced no-knowledge assessment; it still does not admit an empty graph.
decisions.reason: Prevents incomplete or unsupported assessments from being treated as successful.
decisions.text: A successful review requires a complete validated assessment. Missing assessments, invented citations, contradictions, omissions, distortions, or insufficient context cannot pass. Empty extraction requires explicit evidence that the source contains no relevant knowledge, and does not thereby qualify an empty graph for admission.

conditions: Auto emits progress only when stderr is a terminal.
exceptions: Never suppresses progress but preserves error diagnostics.
decisions.reason: Keeps machine-readable results separate from optional human-readable progress.
decisions.text: Update, repair, ask, and review support auto, always, and never progress modes. Auto emits progress only when stderr is a terminal; progress is written to stderr, while final JSON stays on stdout. Progress is a human-readable aid, not a stable event protocol.

exceptions: An abruptly killed process may emit no final checkpoint.
decisions.reason: Makes progress useful without overstating completion or exposing source and model content.
decisions.text: Progress checkpoints describe retained work transitions: extracted units remain pending until checking and admission finish, and admission may preserve uncertainty or findings. Checkpoints distinguish cached results from new calls and report elapsed wait time without claiming internal model progress. They omit source text, prompts, responses, and reasoning; abrupt termination may prevent a final checkpoint, in which case recovery is the inspection path.

conditions: Use these labels when they help coordination.
decisions.reason: Distinguishes participation expectations from readiness and authorization.
decisions.text: Use AFK when the stated work can finish without further owner participation and HITL when owner participation is expected before completion, where helpful for coordination. Neither grants permission or replaces readiness.

decisions.reason: Records an interim toolchain boundary later clarified as incomplete migration.
decisions.text: The initial native delivery temporarily retained Bun and TypeScript for tests and packaging.

conditions: Supplied decision references must use valid exact IDs.
decisions.reason: Protects retained knowledge and relationships while distinguishing interpretation correction from policy change.
decisions.text: Repair packets include current interpretations as comparison context, not authority. Replacements retain correct knowledge and supported dependencies, rewiring changed endpoints; correcting a model interpretation is not a source-authored policy supersession. Unchanged supplied decisions may be referenced by exact IDs; invalid references are rejected, and this context counts toward the limit.

decisions.reason: Defines work-type labels by their function rather than by workflow tooling.
decisions.text: Use useful work-type labels for the kind of work; epic groups coherent child work, while research, prototype, and decision identify work that resolves uncertainty. These labels do not depend on a particular skill.

conditions: The comparison uses the work-start baseline, including after resumption.
decisions.reason: Defines warning-change reporting without conflating source freshness with closure status or implying the entire backlog was reviewed.
decisions.text: warningChanges describes changes seen by one work: new IDs were absent at its start; resolved IDs lacked a closure then and ended with one; reopened IDs had earlier closures whose evidence became stale before or during the work, and remain reopened until revalidated. The baseline records closure status independently of source coverage and survives resumption. A current-source closure may precede ingestion. Review new active and reopened entries against current sources; this report is not a cleanup of the full backlog.

conditions: The replacement workflow is the applicable workflow.
exceptions: Historical evidence and its actual results and limits remain records; they are not erased or upgraded into current obligations.
decisions.reason: Separates the replacement product contract from the retired implementation ceremony while preserving its history.
decisions.text: The replacement workflow supersedes the former mandatory candidate, fidelity, pair-comparison, admission, and grounding ceremony in ADRs 0004–0009. Those ADRs remain historical records of the earlier implementation, retaining their actual results and limits; their old code, graph, suite, or machinery need not define the replacement architecture or acceptance target.

conditions: Requests were complete and within the plan limit before store access or model invocation.
The store was separate from candidate ingestion.
exceptions: Freed pages could be reused after retirement.
decisions.reason: Bounded and separated resumable review work from source and graph authority.
decisions.text: The former source-review cohort used a separate local SQLite store, not documentary authority, bounded by its plan, source, result, and database limits. Prepare every complete source request before opening the store or invoking the model. This describes the legacy review workflow, not a current storage requirement.

conditions: Legacy warnings remain unclassified unless evidence establishes their category.
decisions.reason: Keeps evidence limits, validation outcomes, and knowledge quality distinct.
decisions.text: Warning summaries distinguish extraction limitations, check findings, local validation errors, and unclassified legacy warnings; source counts represent discovery or ingestion limits. A limitation alone does not make a completed update partial, and coverage is separate from interpretation quality. The graph captures meaningful decisions and dependencies rather than every source detail.

conditions: Applies to projects adopting Hivex.
decisions.reason: Keeps source ownership with the adopting project.
decisions.text: An adopting project retains its own Markdown at monorepo, package, or module scope; Hivex does not own that source tree.

decisions.reason: Keeps implementation risk distinct from security finding severity and tool choices.
decisions.text: High-risk calls attention to consequential changes but does not select a vendor or model or prescribe a review count. Security severity labels describe finding severity, distinct from implementation risk.

conditions: Preserve field ordering where compatibility requires it.
decisions.reason: Protects the work representation's invariants and compatibility during refactoring.
decisions.text: Internal Work operations own mutations to the v1 representation. Typed states and phases protect invariants, while boundary serialization preserves absent optional fields, retained errors, and field ordering where compatibility requires it. A domain refactor does not authorize a data migration or reset.

exceptions: Read-only retrieval does not require an issue.
Do not require additional specification structure for work already defined.
decisions.reason: Makes issue creation and specification proportionate to scope and actionability.
decisions.text: Read the relevant issue, discussion, and dependencies. Reuse an issue when its scope covers the request or finding; create a separate issue when work is independently actionable or cannot fit the current scope. Read-only retrieval needs no new issue. Describe the outcome, boundaries, and useful acceptance evidence; split work when that helps verification, without requiring a separate spec, long user-story list, or decision-map hierarchy for already-defined work.

exceptions: Real Luna evaluations are separate from simulated test results.
decisions.reason: Distinguishes compatibility tests and simulated usage from measured real evaluations.
decisions.text: Tests exercise the public CLI and simulated native transport; the CLI suite requires the native binary and has no fallback to another implementation. Synthetic model tests use no real model calls, and simulated token usage is not a consumption measurement. Real Luna evaluations are bounded and reported separately.

conditions: Applies to project-specific glossary entries.
exceptions: Context-specific definitions may be linked rather than repeated.
decisions.reason: Keeps the glossary focused on shared project language.
decisions.text: Define project-specific glossary concepts briefly and use terms consistently. A glossary is not an implementation manual, task plan, or collection of generic programming terms; group related concepts and link context-specific definitions instead of copying them.

decisions.reason: Keeps the store's scope distinct from downstream graph and grounding requirements.
decisions.text: The ingestion-store decision governs bounded storage only; it does not itself provide graph assembly, admission, historical evidence, or implementation grounding.

decisions.reason: Keeps source fidelity distinct from other forms of validation.
decisions.text: Source-fidelity review does not establish cross-source consistency, effective authority, graph admission, or implementation grounding; those remain separate requirements.

conditions: Main-branch integration is subject to the stated PR, check, and review-conversation requirements.
exceptions: Do not require a second person's approval on owner-authored PRs.
decisions.reason: Describes current repository integrity controls and explains why they do not replace per-PR authorization.
decisions.text: The current main-branch controls require a PR, an up-to-date successful GitHub Actions quality check, and resolved review conversations; force pushes and deletion are blocked. Only the owner's account currently has write access, and public visibility grants neither write nor merge access. Do not require another person's approval on owner-authored PRs because GitHub disallows self-approval. Account controls cannot distinguish the owner from tools using the owner's credentials, so agents must still follow the per-PR authorization rule.

conditions: Visibility checks apply to the first GitHub Packages publication.
decisions.reason: Distinguishes package visibility from registry download authentication.
decisions.text: For the first GitHub Packages publication, verify repository association and visibility. GitHub packages start private even when linked to a public repository; set the package public before claiming visitors can see it. Downloading from GitHub's npm registry still requires authentication, while npmjs.org remains available without that requirement.

conditions: The objection was evaluated against the actual supplied claim.
exceptions: A genuine change in meaning or conflict in applicability could support an ambiguity finding.
decisions.reason: Prevented fidelity objections from inventing metadata or ambiguity not present in the claim.
decisions.text: In the former comparison workflow, repeating a consistent scope in a statement and its conditions or exceptions did not by itself make the claim ambiguous. An objection required identifying changed meaning or conflicting applicability in the supplied claim.

exceptions: Legacy and evidence collections may be excluded from an individual retrieval query.
decisions.reason: Separates authored status metadata and retrieval selection from a semantic determination of authority.
decisions.text: Declared status and replacement references are exposed, but effective currentness is reported as unestablished; an Accepted label alone does not resolve amendments, exceptions, or conflicts. Legacy and evidence collections are opt-in, and omitting them from retrieval does not revoke their authority.

conditions: The in-memory FTS5 index uses up to 32 shared terms per source, ranked by document frequency and term, then BM25 with source ID as tie-breaker; no more than the requested number of outgoing candidates are retained.
exceptions: Incoming selections may give a source additional neighbors.
decisions.reason: Adds bounded candidate discovery while making its deterministic behavior and retrieval limitations explicit.
decisions.text: Optional lexical-neighbor selection accepts values from 1 to 8; zero remains the default and preserves the authored-link plan unchanged. It adds deterministic candidates using shared terms and FTS5 ranking, deduplicates source pairs, and retains authored reasons. Its settings affect the selection hash, not the model request, which still assesses complete sources. This retrieval heuristic neither establishes semantic relationships nor provides full coverage; sources with no shared terms remain counted.

conditions: The complexity gate uses source function spaces and the published Mozilla analyzer.
exceptions: Only standalone initializer closures receive the stated wrapper; control flow is not rewritten to work around parser limits.
decisions.reason: Makes the metric implementation and per-function interpretation reproducible while failing closed on unsupported bodies.
decisions.text: Use Mozilla `rust-code-analysis` version 0.0.25 rather than a handwritten complexity algorithm. The quality gate validates whole files with `syn`, locates original function and method spans with `proc-macro2`, then measures those unmodified spans with Mozilla; an initializer closure may receive only a `const` wrapper, and unsupported function bodies fail. Measure each function space's local cognitive and cyclomatic scores, recursing into child spaces rather than using file totals, maxima, or averages. Keep the compatible Tree-sitter API resolution locked.

conditions: The reviewer remains responsible for acceptance.
decisions.reason: Defines the skills as assistance rather than an approval mechanism or mandatory workflow.
decisions.text: Use the workflow skills and capabilities a task needs rather than following a compulsory sequence. No installed command approves an implementation; the principal reviewer checks findings, relevant tests, and source evidence and retains acceptance responsibility.

conditions: Results are retained only for the recorded claimant.
exceptions: Unresolved invocations cannot be automatically retried or discarded.
decisions.reason: Protects concurrent work and preserves truthful invocation and assessment state.
decisions.text: Claim each pending source atomically before model invocation, invoke outside the transaction, and retain the full result only for the claimant. Resume without repeating completed work. An interrupted invocation remains unresolved and cannot be automatically retried or discarded; retain known usage and make unknown usage explicit. A retained negative assessment remains negative on resume.

conditions: Retained results are reusable only while their source and processing context match.
exceptions: Caches optimize work but have no authority.
decisions.reason: Makes ingestion resumable and bounded while preserving partial progress and source authority.
decisions.text: Updates split oversized Markdown into source-bound units with original line provenance, process bounded rounds, checkpoint progress, and reuse retained results only when source and processing context match. Each update has one bounded additional knowledge check; it does not exhaustively inspect every node or source pair or retry automatically for a green result. Usable knowledge remains available with pending or uncertain limits visible, and derived interpretations can be corrected against sources without changing doctrine.

conditions: Applies to production domain modules.
exceptions: None stated.
decisions.reason: Keeps domain boundaries concrete and prevents consumers from depending on internal implementation files.
decisions.text: Use a modular monolith with private production submodules and no hexagonal layers or empty interfaces. Each domain root reexports the concrete types and operations consumers need; callers do not reach into another domain's storage, parser, protocol, or other implementation files.

decisions.reason: Limits what readiness labels imply.
decisions.text: Keep readiness coherent: it does not promise that all later decisions are settled, choose a model, or override an unresolved dependency.

conditions: Applies to runtime code, development utilities, and tests.
exceptions: The 100-column setting is a formatting target, not a byte-length prohibition; rustfmt may retain long literals or macro input, and nightly formatting options are unnecessary.
decisions.reason: Defines a maintained Rust baseline while protecting readability and behavior.
decisions.text: The approved Rust standard applies to runtime code, development utilities, and tests. Use stable Rust, rustfmt, and Clippy. Formatting uses two spaces, no hard tabs, and a 100-column target; preserve behavior and readable responsibilities when refactoring rather than changing design merely to affect a metric.

decisions.reason: Records CI verification and dependency/distribution boundaries.
decisions.text: The Quality workflow runs the gates on its existing GitHub-hosted macOS ARM64 runner and verifies native package and CLI contracts; these gates make no model calls. Distribution excludes the analyzer and development-only utilities, and package notices follow normal and build dependency edges rather than development-only edges. `num-traits` is an explicit runtime dependency for checked numeric conversions, with v1 numeric behavior protected by existing contracts.

conditions: Evaluate applicable decision/amendment regression before declaring the cycle complete.
exceptions: Admission alone is not code approval or doctrinal resolution.
decisions.reason: Limits what admission proves and identifies the additional implementation-grounding work required.
decisions.text: Admission establishes recorded coverage, not exhaustive semantic consistency across every possible source pair. It does not approve code or resolve doctrine; applicable decisions and amendments, including their conditions, must be grounded against the exact implementation, and applicable decision/amendment regressions must be evaluated before declaring that cycle complete.

conditions: Repeated transition uses the same complete archive binding.
exceptions: An older transition lacking the binding may continue through ordinary resume but cannot authenticate a repeated transfer.
decisions.reason: Ensures transitions are tied to the predecessor evidence they replace.
decisions.text: A repeated transition under the format-2 archive binding is accepted only for the same complete predecessor plan and archived rows; an altered archive or separately initialized destination is rejected. Older transitions without that binding cannot authenticate a repeated transfer, so continue their current cohort through ordinary resume. Transition and migration share a transaction and cannot cross an active claim; retirement and subsequent cohort initialization clear the binding.

conditions: Each complete repair range must fit the existing round bound.
exceptions: Unexecuted plans may use a more precise scope.
decisions.reason: Preserves precise repair scope and accounting without breaking decision citations.
decisions.text: Range repair selects requested passages and complete overlapping decision citations, not the entire physical ingestion block, while preserving unrelated decisions and relationships. Each complete range must fit the round byte bound; do not split a decision to fit. Executed or pending work retains its ranges and accounting, while unexecuted plans may use more precise scope. A broader completed repair remains reusable for its original request.

conditions: Applies when organizing project knowledge.
exceptions: Research may support a decision but does not become one automatically.
decisions.reason: Helps readers distinguish document purposes and evidence from active decisions.
decisions.text: A useful catalogue gives distinct roles to an authority map, PRD, glossary, decisions, guidelines, procedures, and research. Research is dated supporting evidence, not automatically a current decision.

exceptions: Unit tests may access private production modules.
decisions.reason: Maintains domain boundaries and tests behavior through the supported CLI surface.
decisions.text: Follow the modular monolith and domain boundaries. Keep modules cohesive and private by default: discovery and Markdown parsing stay independent of knowledge, review, and model execution; ingestion may use documents; review may use documents and knowledge; execution contracts stay vendor-independent; and work, consultation, integrations, and CLI compose those responsibilities at their stated boundaries. Unit tests may use private production modules, but production cannot import tests. CLI integration tests use the compiled executable, fixed v1 SQL fixtures, and a synthetic Rust app-server. The development utility and synthetic server are separate, undistributed binaries.

conditions: Existing SQLite data is preserved without reingestion.
exceptions: Consumer knowledge is never migrated in place merely to make a test pass.
decisions.reason: Protects compatibility, recoverability, and consumer-data boundaries through runtime migration.
decisions.text: Migration preserves observable CLI behavior, source coordinates and hashes, snapshot v1, existing SQLite data, knowledge identities and history, caches, unfinished or failed work, results, and cumulative budgets including unknown consumption. Compatibility checks use synthetic public fixtures and simulated native transport; consumer knowledge stays private. Native Codex compatibility is capability-based with localized model selection and no silent fallback.

conditions: Every invocation in both works must have completed with confirmed acceptance and cleanup; recovery acknowledgement is insufficient.
The replacement must be complete with no pending stage.
exceptions: Supersession does not admit the old candidate, resolve graph warnings, or certify graph quality; semantic adequacy remains the reviewer's responsibility.
Only the superseded work ceases to block snapshot import or relocation; other unfinished work remains a blocker.
decisions.reason: Closes obsolete work only when an attributable, current, completed replacement covers its objectives while retaining the failed record.
decisions.text: A failed update with a staged candidate and completed last check can be explicitly superseded by a completed replacement update. The source-backed review must identify both works and the check, give a bounded reason, and provide current versioned evidence for every affected document. The replacement's uniquely attributable current coverage units must be in its original plan and cover every remaining or staged target at the original still-current versions; ambiguity, missing ranges or versions, or lost attribution cause refusal. The operation acquires the update lease and records the disposition atomically. It preserves the failed status, candidate, attempts, results, and budgets. Exact replay is idempotent; another disposition is rejected. A superseded work cannot resume, retry, change profile, correct, or resolve its candidate, and both records are protected from pruning.

conditions: When work produces a decision worth preserving.
exceptions: Issues may track work and discussion, but do not replace the canonical documentation.
decisions.reason: Preserves decisions in an appropriate, maintainable authoritative location.
decisions.text: Record durable decisions in the appropriate repository document; update the existing canonical source when it already owns the topic. Keep documentation with the monorepo, workspace, or module it describes, and link common rules rather than copying them. Compatible existing Markdown need not adopt a recommended template; do not create empty documentation for every module or expand scope to non-Markdown readers.

conditions: Work must have ready scope and resolved actual blockers to be selectable.
decisions.reason: Connects selection and requests for clarification to evidence, scope, and blockers rather than labels alone.
decisions.text: Apply triage labels consistently. Work is selectable when its scope is ready and actual blockers are resolved. Labels neither authorize external actions nor select a model. Ask only for decisions or information that existing evidence cannot recover.

conditions: A timeout retry requires confirmed interruption and remains within the three-attempt limit.
exceptions: Invalid extraction output may be corrected with explicit feedback; an adverse grounded review may not be rerolled.
decisions.reason: Maintains reliable attempt accounting and prevents unsafe retry or verdict-selection behavior.
decisions.text: Each invocation has a finite deadline and is recorded as one attempt. Preserve known usage on failure and leave missing usage unknown. Retry a timeout only after interruption is confirmed, with no more than three attempts; an unconfirmed start or interruption is failure, not proof no request occurred.
