Invalid extraction output may receive explicit corrective feedback, but an adverse grounded review must not be rerolled for a preferred verdict.

conditions: Cover useful capabilities and active callers before retiring superseded general skills.
exceptions: Unrelated technical specialties remain separate.
Handoff requires no dedicated skill or reference.
decisions.reason: Keeps reusable guidance compact while preserving useful capabilities, scope, and authorization.
decisions.text: Keep skills focused, with conditional references that preserve user scope and existing authorization. Replace superseded general skills only after covering useful capabilities and active callers. The clarified replacement covers the former external general set, including generic personal, writing, and provider-specific utilities; retain only non-obvious guidance that improves the workflow, and keep unrelated technical specialties separate. Do not recreate the old catalogue, prescribe arbitrary line limits, or add tutorials for capabilities the model already provides. Handoff needs no dedicated skill or reference.

conditions: When changing or reviewing tests.
exceptions: Mocks, call counts, ordering, and exact bytes may remain when they protect a contract.
decisions.reason: Tests should protect behavior that matters, not merely mirror current internal structure.
decisions.text: Test doubles and implementation-level assertions are appropriate when they protect a real contract, such as an external protocol or query budget. Review existing tests for retention, rewriting, consolidation, or removal; preserve active guarantees at the replacement interface rather than mechanically porting legacy tests or targeting a test count.

conditions: An identical move may reuse ingestion coverage only when the source is unchanged.
Changed or consolidated content requires the normal update/check at the destination.
exceptions: Relocation is refused while local work is unfinished.
decisions.reason: Keeps evidence and work history auditable across document moves without implying approval or freshness.
decisions.text: Explicit source relocation preserves decision and relationship identities, source versions, uncertainty, and work history. An identical move may reuse ingestion coverage without a model call; changed content or consolidation requires the normal destination update/check, and relocation does not approve an interpretation or make mismatched evidence current. Refuse relocation while local work is unfinished, preserve original work and model answers, record source, destination, and versions in the operation report, and commit the exported graph with the corresponding source changes.

conditions: Applies when interpreting coverage of the source complexity metrics and syntax gates.
exceptions: Written macro tokens may be checked for specific syntax or dependency rules, but macro expansion is not analyzed.
decisions.reason: States analyzer blind spots so source-metric results are not mistaken for expanded-code coverage.
decisions.text: These are source metrics, not measurements of expanded or optimized compiler output. Mozilla does not expand macros, so code and control flow inside opaque macro input are not counted as measured function spaces. Keep substantial executable macro arguments in ordinary Rust functions or local expressions and review generated behavior. Syntax and dependency gates can inspect written macro tokens for their specific rules, but do not expand macros; Cargo check and Clippy remain compiler validation. Clippy's experimental cognitive-complexity lint is not an equivalent replacement.

decisions.reason: Sets the current implementation context and avoids duplicating host coordination or imposing Hivex's structure on adopters.
decisions.text: Hivex is currently a Rust CLI migrated under issue 80 and ADR 0010. Fixed v1 fixtures and public CLI tests preserve prior runtime contracts. Organize modules by domain responsibility behind small interfaces; do not add another development-session orchestrator or require adopting projects to use Hivex's layout, tracker, or product packages. Codex, Git/GitHub, and CI coordinate work.

decisions.reason: Defines update and repair work while preserving source authority and bounded checking.
decisions.text: A knowledge update processes selected document versions into decisions and relationships, followed by one bounded source check. A knowledge check looks for omissions and misinterpretations rather than certifying global completeness. Interpretation repair corrects derived knowledge against unchanged Markdown, but does not resolve a genuine policy conflict. Source relocation retains existing knowledge and links while distinguishing reusable evidence from content needing a new check.

exceptions: Conventional Commits are a useful default, not an overriding project convention.
decisions.reason: Keeps implementation coherent and avoids unnecessary orchestration.
decisions.text: Start implementation from the current integration branch and keep changes coherent. Follow project commit conventions, with Conventional Commits as a useful default. Prefer existing checks and native Git or tracker capabilities over an additional orchestration layer.

decisions.reason: Preserves result provenance across model generations; the current guide likewise keeps prior-profile results distinct from new-profile results.
decisions.text: Do not relabel old Opus payloads as Luna results.

decisions.reason: Records current test and CI organization.
decisions.text: Current CI runs unit tests in the development build and the complete CLI contracts once against the packaged release executable. The parser matrix belongs beside the parser, and Codex-specific protocol tests belong in tests/contracts/codex.rs.

decisions.reason: Prevents coverage state and different kinds of warning from being conflated.
decisions.text: The graph retrieves decisions, dependencies, and exceptions rather than reproducing every Markdown detail. Distinguish evidence limits from check findings and local validation failures, preserve legacy warnings without guessing their category, and treat coverage and interpretation quality as separate.

conditions: Working state and exact contents must be identifiable.
decisions.reason: Makes analysis version-specific while permitting work on uncommitted documents.
decisions.text: Consultations and reviews detect added, changed, and removed Markdown, update affected knowledge within budget, and reuse unchanged knowledge. Working documents are readable without a commit if their working state and exact contents are identifiable. Results refer to the document and implementation versions actually considered; later changes are not covered silently.

conditions: Export evidence first if historical reports are needed.
exceptions: Pruning is explicit and does not reset a work budget.
decisions.reason: Bounds stored history without deleting active work or its accounting.
decisions.text: Pruning explicitly releases old completed work and cached results while retaining the graph and all unfinished work, attempts, and budgets. It protects completed replacements referenced by supersession and, by default, retains the newest eight other completed works and 64 cached results; options can change those counts. Pruned answers may require a new model call.

conditions: The complete relationship context must fit the configured context limit before extraction begins.
exceptions: A line too large to fit is reported unread, never silently truncated.
decisions.reason: Bounds ingestion while preserving source coordinates and required relationship evidence.
decisions.text: Updates split large Markdown into line-preserving units of at most 8 KiB, preferring Markdown boundaries. A round selects at most four units and 16 KiB of target text, then performs one additional check. Optional neighbor discovery is bounded, but current affected endpoints and their evidence remain required; if the complete packet exceeds the context limit, report it before extraction. Sources may be split up to 32 MiB within a 64 MiB loaded-corpus limit; a line that cannot fit is reported unread rather than cut.

decisions.reason: Keeps policy, knowledge state, and host execution responsibilities separate.
decisions.text: Keep task guidance in skills, agent coordination and execution mechanics in the host harness, workflow policy in project Markdown, and knowledge state and work accounting in Hivex's CLI. Do not reproduce harness responsibilities throughout skills.

conditions: Publication requires approval for the concrete archive and an authorized npm account.
decisions.reason: Binds publication authorization to the exact checked artifact.
decisions.text: Obtain publication approval for the concrete archive, confirm an npm account authorized for the scope, and publish the same checked tarball. Approval for an earlier version does not authorize another artifact.

conditions: Cleanup applies to work that is finished; implementation changes must first be integrated.
exceptions: Completed research, evidence, or prototypes may be cleaned up after their useful results and required history are retained.
Unfinished or uncertain work remains intact; unmerged work requires an established disposition and applicable owner authorization before discard.
decisions.reason: Protects retained work and history while making integration a prerequisite for treating implementation as complete.
decisions.text: Clean up branches and worktrees only for finished work. Implementation changes must be integrated before they count as completed work for cleanup; retain useful results and required history for completed research, evidence, or prototypes first. Keep unfinished or uncertain work intact regardless of age or PR status. Do not discard unmerged work without an established disposition and applicable owner authorization.

conditions: Use additional planning stages or tickets when the work needs them.
exceptions: A defined change need not acquire additional stages or tickets.
decisions.reason: Encourages useful design and planning without imposing ceremony or architecture for its own sake.
decisions.text: Prefer Domain-Driven Design and meaningful module responsibilities without requiring hexagonal architecture or speculative abstractions. Use the planning and tracking capabilities a change needs; stages and extra tickets are not compulsory when the change is already defined.

decisions.reason: Distinguishes preparing a foundation from adapting it to a project.
decisions.text: A project foundation is a set of starter documents, workflow capabilities, and knowledge practices tailored by the adopting project. Initialization prepares missing foundation files without adding project facts or replacing existing knowledge; adoption completes and aligns the foundation while preserving useful existing knowledge.

conditions: The old source is no longer selected and the destination is selected current Markdown.
Coverage reuse requires no prior destination knowledge and matching known versions for all retained evidence.
There must be no unfinished local work.
exceptions: Changed content, mixed or missing evidence versions, or existing destination knowledge makes coverage pending for validation.
decisions.reason: Preserves knowledge and local accounting while making source moves verifiable.
decisions.text: Relocation requires the old source to be unselected and the destination to be selected current Markdown. It preserves identities, relationships, versions, uncertainty, work, cached answers, and budgets, makes no model calls, and refuses unfinished local work. Ingestion coverage is reusable only when the destination has no prior knowledge and all retained evidence has matching known versions; otherwise coverage becomes pending for validation. Keep the relocation report and export the final graph; relocation must not hide unrelated missing evidence.

conditions: The result is reused only while supplied context remains unchanged.
decisions.reason: Defines bounded, resumable consultation behavior.
decisions.text: A consultation maintains at most one bounded pending batch before answering, prioritizes matching fragments and known affected neighbors, and shares one work budget across update, check, and answer. Context-limit increases do not reset unfinished work; remaining coverage is reported and explicit updates can advance it. Repeating a completed consultation reuses its result when supplied context is unchanged.

conditions: The harness must support workflow policy retained in project Markdown.
exceptions: Removing duplicated skill instructions does not configure the harness.
decisions.reason: Separates task guidance, host execution responsibilities, and Hivex CLI contracts.
decisions.text: Skills provide reusable domain knowledge and criteria; the host harness coordinates agents, applies model and effort configuration, and manages permissions, processes, and session limits. Skills must not implement a parallel orchestration or permission layer. Project Markdown retains workflow policy, including independent review and model/effort matching, and the harness must support it; removing duplicated skill instructions does not configure the harness. Hivex's CLI owns its versioned evidence, persisted budgets, recovery, and uncertainty; its skill retains the conditions for correct use and directs advanced mechanics to the CLI manual.

conditions: A context handoff is needed for the task.
decisions.reason: Keeps context handoffs need-based rather than tied to retired fixed thresholds.
decisions.text: Choose a context handoff when the task needs one; Hivex imposes no fixed token thresholds from the retired workflow.

exceptions: No repository interface is required for every entity.
decisions.reason: Defines capability ownership and keeps persistence near the behavior it serves.
decisions.text: Assign behavior by capability: Documents owns source discovery, parsing, and coordinates; Knowledge owns the derived graph, retrieval, ingestion, relationships, warnings, repairs, and snapshots; Work owns progress, attempts, budgets, transitions, and recovery. Consultation and review compose those capabilities; CLI parsing and process exit/output belong at the entry boundary. Concrete SQLite persistence stays beside the behavior it serves, without requiring a repository interface for every entity.

decisions.reason: Distinguishes the graph projection from completion of the larger admission workflow.
decisions.text: Full reconstruction with Luna/max, semantic evaluation, admission, and implementation grounding remain requirements of the graph-admission workflow; defining the projection does not declare those gates delivered.

conditions: Endpoint changes require the source passages supporting prior relationships.
exceptions: Removed sources remain identifiable when a dependency can no longer be verified.
decisions.reason: Keeps repairs source-bound, scoped, and inspectable.
decisions.text: Repair revisits selected source units with a correction reason but does not edit Markdown. It replaces derived decisions and relationships while preserving prior attempts. Findings carry source, version, and range scope; changed known supporting sources take priority, and missing relationship evidence keeps work pending with the limitation reported before a model call.

conditions: Applies when removing old logs or current files.
exceptions: Changing repository visibility is not part of this cleanup.
decisions.reason: Preserves useful evidence while distinguishing current cleanup from historical or publication records.
decisions.text: Before deleting old Actions logs containing workstation details, preserve needed historical verification privately. Retain Git history, attribution, and useful decisions; recognize that deleting current files or logs does not remove historical commits or published packages. Treat a visibility change as a separate explicit action.

decisions.reason: Describes the current project tracker and language/convention setup.
decisions.text: The current tracker setup uses GitHub issues and pull requests in H1V35/hivex with `gh`. Work is issue-first, with a coherent branch and PR per change. Tracker and PR text and commit messages are Spanish; code, branches, and repository Markdown are English. Commits and PR titles use an emoji followed by a Conventional Commit type or scope and a Spanish description.

conditions: The test's guarantee must be preserved elsewhere unless its behavior is retired.
decisions.reason: Prevents losing meaningful test coverage during suite changes.
decisions.text: Remove a test only when its meaningful guarantee is retained elsewhere or the tested behavior has been retired.

conditions: Use archive globs for historical sources intended for focused retrieval.
exceptions: Existing `history` configuration remains readable; it cannot be specified together with `archive`.
decisions.reason: Enables portable snapshot reuse and selective historical retrieval without losing existing work or cache state.
decisions.text: The CLI supports explicit snapshot export and import, including reuse in a fresh clone. Configurable archive globs keep historical sources available for focused retrieval while excluding them from ordinary ingestion. The former `history` field remains a read-compatible alias, but specifying it together with `archive` is invalid; renaming preserves source identities, work accounting, and retained caches.

conditions: Call and input-byte limits apply to the complete work, including resumptions.
exceptions: A completed adverse check is not an invocation failure and is not repeated for an unchanged candidate.
The local store has a 64 MiB bound; source Markdown is not rewritten.
decisions.reason: Preserves progress and accountable work history while preventing implicit retries or budget resets.
decisions.text: An explicit update has a cumulative work budget, by default two invocation attempts and 131,072 input bytes, covering the complete work and its resumptions. Exhaustion preserves progress; zero-call updates report pending documents, and an authorized larger total can resume remaining stages without repeating completed extraction. Failed or unfinished invocations are not retried automatically: inspect the result first, retry only safely ended failures with the explicit retry option and within the same budget, and keep uncertain invocations blocked. The local SQLite store holds working knowledge and execution accounting; preserve it when evidence is needed and do not delete an active store to hide work or reset its budget.

conditions: The evidence scope must match the finding's target and use current supplied sources.
Batch and document targets are eligible only for materialized checks; a document target must be a current document supplied to that check.
exceptions: Do not use this process for a real contradiction or missing dependency.
decisions.reason: Allows source-backed review of false findings without bypassing candidate integrity or relationship safeguards.
decisions.text: A false semantic finding blocking a retained repair candidate can be disposed of locally against the exact completed check and current canonical candidate, without a model call. A document disposition must cite that document; a batch disposition must cite every pending target range. The work, check, candidate, graph, and sources must remain unchanged. Unknown targets, structural failures, and unsupported evidence remain blocking, and protected relationships still require supported replacements or removals. The disposition preserves the original findings and usage and is a reviewed judgement, not proof of correctness.

conditions: Include conditions, exceptions, dependencies, or replacements when they affect application.
exceptions: No fixed set of optional sections is required.
decisions.reason: Makes decisions usable without turning their format into empty ceremony.
decisions.text: A decision should state what was decided and why, including scope, application-changing conditions or exceptions, and relevant dependencies or replacements. Use optional sections only when they add information; a short paragraph can suffice.

exceptions: A shared snapshot is not required when an existing local store is used.
decisions.reason: Protects snapshot integrity and local knowledge during read-only and invalid-input operations.
decisions.text: Read-only queries do not rewrite the snapshot; export intentionally when reusable knowledge changes rather than on every consultation. Invalid snapshots and symbolic-link paths fail without replacing local knowledge. An existing local store can be used without a shared snapshot.

conditions: Other targets require native compatibility validation before distribution.
decisions.reason: States the current platform and runtime boundary without implying broader compatibility.
decisions.text: The native package currently targets macOS ARM64. Its installed executable does not require Bun, Node.js, or Rust; npm or Bun is needed only for package installation.

conditions: A closure requires an explicit reason and current evidence.
exceptions: A genuine unresolved question need not be answered or closed.
Manual evidence-backed dispositions remain permitted, but do not substitute for repair of a real implementation or relationship defect.
decisions.reason: Allows explicit, source-backed dispositions without treating an adverse check or validation result as proof of resolution.
decisions.text: Close warnings only with an explicit reason and current evidence, using warnings --resolve for an evidence-backed disposition; preserve prior closures. A changed or unavailable cited source reactivates its warning. Manual disposition remains possible, but actual implementation or relationship defects require correction or repair, and findings or local validation failures do not themselves justify closure. Leave genuine unresolved questions open; do not repeat a model to obtain a green result or scan the whole corpus to chase zero warnings.

conditions: Any subsequent retry follows the retained work budget and safe-failure rules.
exceptions: An acknowledgement is not proof that the remote turn completed.
decisions.reason: Separates recovery bookkeeping from proof of execution or permission to retry.
decisions.text: Recovery inspects abandoned work without invoking the model or terminating live owners or native processes. When local processes ended but remote delivery is uncertain, an explicit acknowledgement records that uncertainty; original reports and unknown usage remain visible. Recovery itself never retries work.

decisions.reason: Defines the graph's content and provenance without making it a source of authority.
decisions.text: A decision captures a meaningful choice or constraint with its scope, conditions, exceptions, reasons, and declared state. A relationship is an evidenced connection between decisions, including implicit cross-document links, and may be uncertain. Evidence identifies an inspectable passage of a particular source version. The derived knowledge graph may be incomplete or uncertain; a knowledge snapshot packages reusable graph knowledge with its source versions, evidence, provenance, and coverage, separately from document snapshots and execution state.

conditions: For package release and project integration.
exceptions: Do not infer npm ownership from a matching GitHub name.
decisions.reason: Sets the chosen distribution identity and boundaries without implying a completed release.
decisions.text: The selected npm package is `@h1v35/hivex`, with `hivex` as the installed command and MIT licensing. Use an account authorized for the package scope. Verify packed contents and exclude private project evidence and runtime stores; project integration follows the normal release process after the complete cycle is validated. The selection does not establish that publication has occurred.

conditions: The request and receipt or inspection input each fit within 256 KiB.
exceptions: Reassociated receipts could not substitute for the original comparison evidence.
decisions.reason: Preserved feedback provenance and bounded the former standalone reassessment input.
decisions.text: For the former comparison-feedback review, input could be the complete original comparison receipt or a single-pair inspection file, using the original graph; a reassociated receipt required returning to its original evidence. The input and complete source-and-concern prompt each had to fit the stated bound. The resulting review retained the full original comparison and hash, including usage, and bound its request to the receipt identity and selected feedback. Preparation made no model call.

exceptions: Bun’s native controls were not represented as equivalent to every former pnpm policy.
decisions.reason: This installation approach was part of the Bun requirements explicitly superseded by the Rust migration.
decisions.text: The historical installation design relied on Bun rather than a Hivex-maintained installer, publishing-trust verifier, registry cache, or generated bootstrap, and allowed Hivex to run independently of caller package managers. It did not claim parity with every former pnpm policy.

conditions: Changed or new pairs remained pending, and removed pairs remained in the caller-owned archive.
A repeated completed transition required the exact recorded archive and the store that owned the old cohort.
exceptions: A known preflight failure before any accepted turn remained a failure; adverse assessments were not retried or changed.
decisions.reason: Allowed only compatible reuse while preserving the original comparison, selection provenance, and transition history.
decisions.text: The former comparison transition reused a pair only while it remained selected and its complete request, source descriptors, claim identities, and processing contract were unchanged. Recompute the selection and preserve its reasons; selection ranks and neighbor counts were not model inputs, and reuse did not assess newly selected pairs. Preserve the old graph and export, validate the archive against retained rows, and retain the original comparison and receipt while binding the association to the new graph and selection. Inspection and admission revalidated the association and original inputs. Uncertain starts, unconfirmed interruptions, failed cleanup, and active claims blocked replacement.

conditions: The failure must have ended safely, and the total attempt budget must allow another attempt.
exceptions: Unknown acceptance, unconfirmed interruption, failed cleanup, active claims, and completed semantic assessments are ineligible.
decisions.reason: Provides bounded explicit recovery without changing evidence or fishing for approval.
decisions.text: Explicitly retry only a failed source review or pair comparison whose invocation ended safely: preflight failure before an accepted turn, invalid output after confirmed completion and cleanup, or acknowledged interruption with confirmed cleanup. Preserve the previous receipt and use the same request and contract; retry adds no evidence and does not repair rejected output. Allow at most three total attempts per unit, including earlier attempts. Ordinary resume never retries; adverse findings and insufficient context require addressing their evidence, not seeking a different verdict.

conditions: The native target is limited to the validated macOS ARM64 platform.
decisions.reason: States the validated platform scope without implying broader native compatibility.
decisions.text: The first verified native distribution targets macOS ARM64: npm links directly to the executable, declares OS and CPU, and needs no JavaScript launcher, runtime package dependency, or install hook. This artifact does not claim compatibility for other platforms that could install the Bun package.

decisions.reason: Identifies the prescribed local verification gates.
decisions.text: Local verification comprises formatting, locked all-target checks and Clippy with warnings denied, quality and architecture tests, and the full locked test suite.

decisions.reason: Prevents scaffold content from being mistaken for project-specific decisions.
decisions.text: Initialization supplies a language-neutral foundation, with language-specific standards provided separately as templates. The principal agent establishes the project’s purpose, vision, and language from evidence and owner decisions; draft headings alone do not establish them.

conditions: Any later user-configured model must be supported.
exceptions: The principal agent may use a different model, but project knowledge remains in the project.
decisions.reason: Fixes the validated model profile while allowing localized future configuration.
decisions.text: Luna/max is the selected knowledge model and validated release profile, without silent fallback. Localize model selection and invocation so users can later configure a supported model; do not build a speculative provider framework or rely on a principal agent's private vendor memory for project knowledge.

conditions: Exclusions take precedence over archive selection.
exceptions: The former history field remains readable for existing projects.
decisions.reason: Defines source-selection safety and configuration migration behavior.
decisions.text: An exclude glob overrides archive selection; symlinks are not followed, and protected directories and scope escapes are rejected. The former collections field is rejected with a migration message. Existing projects may still use history; new configuration uses archive, specifying both is an error, and renaming preserves snapshots, retained work, and caches.

conditions: The comparison is completed, adverse, and questions a claim from the reassessed source.
exceptions: A comparison verdict or insufficient comparison context does not itself establish that the candidate needs revision.
decisions.reason: Uses comparison findings only as bounded feedback for an independent source-fidelity assessment.
decisions.text: A standalone source reassessment may use a completed adverse comparison only when it questions at least one claim belonging to that source. Revalidate the comparison's original graph, two distinct sources, processing contract, native receipt, claim coverage, citations, and normalized output hashes. Successful comparisons, transport failures, and concerns only about another source do not qualify. Insufficient comparison context motivates reassessing the candidate against its complete source but is not itself evidence for revision; provide every original claim and local relation with only target-source concerns and citations, and allow the reviewer to uphold the candidate.

conditions: For intent and decisions not made self-explanatory by code.
exceptions: None stated.
decisions.reason: Keeps durable project doctrine in its authoritative sources and makes unresolved evidence explicit.
decisions.text: Code should explain itself through names, structure, and behavior; repository Markdown is authoritative for intent and constraints that code cannot explain. Do not maintain a parallel implementation manual. Accepted status alone does not settle amendments or conflicts, and historical descriptions of owner decisions require provenance checks. Caches, model output, and search results are not authoritative.

conditions: The replacement workflow applies to the explicitly declared model replacement.
Retire the obsolete unversioned cache on work start or resume.
exceptions: Unrelated profile changes remain an explicit mismatch for pending work.
Historical answers remain available with provenance but are not reused as results from the replacement model.
decisions.reason: Preserves work identity, budget, provenance, and recovery safeguards across a declared execution-profile replacement.
decisions.text: Work budgets span phases and attempts; resumption or configuration changes cannot create a fresh allowance. Execution and cache identity include the integration and result-affecting profile. For the explicit GPT-5.6 Luna-to-GPT-6 Luna replacement, the integration declares the replacement and unfinished work must not depend on the former profile; preserve work ID, progress, historical attempts, and consumed budget while recording the transition. Running or uncertain invocations and failed checks retain normal recovery safeguards; unrelated profile changes produce an explicit mismatch. On start or resume, retire the obsolete unversioned cache generation, including custom-profile entries whose hash-only keys do not identify the model. Make cleanup transactional with work preparation and use versioned keys to protect fresh results. Do not affect read-only operations, graph knowledge, work history, attempts, or budgets; retain historical answer provenance without reusing those answers as GPT-6 results. Execution configuration changes alone do not trigger reingestion.

conditions: Link to authorities relevant to the task.
exceptions: The entrypoint does not require every source to be included in every task.
decisions.reason: Makes authority and project guidance discoverable without imposing a proprietary format.
decisions.text: Keep `AGENTS.md` a concise entrypoint for orientation, development or verification guidance, and relevant project-specific constraints. Links identify when an authority matters without requiring every source for every task. Supply a recommended ordinary-Markdown shape, not a proprietary schema or line-count limit.

conditions: The complete request must fit within 256 KiB and be prepared before claiming.
exceptions: Preparation-only inspection does not mutate state or call the model.
decisions.reason: Makes revision inputs inspectable while preventing omitted evidence from entering the model request.
decisions.text: Prepare the complete revision request before claiming work. Include the original source, prior candidate, claim and relation identities, and review findings as untrusted evidence. Do not truncate the request; its limit is 256 KiB. A preparation-only command exposes it without changing state or invoking the model.

conditions: Resumption or reuse uses the same task and base revision.
A saved report applies only while the considered code and documents remain unchanged.
exceptions: Large changes may need to be narrowed or split into coherent reviews.
decisions.reason: Makes review scope, budget, version applicability, and human acceptance responsibility explicit.
decisions.text: A review uses its task and base revision and captures working changes, including untracked files; findings refer to the code and Markdown versions considered. Resumption or reuse uses the same task and base, and review, update, knowledge check, and report expansion share one budget. Context is bounded, so large changes may need coherent narrowing or splitting. The principal reviewer verifies conflicts and exceptions; a ready result is assistance, not approval. A saved report can be checked without a model but becomes stale if its code or documents change; keep it outside the project or in an ignored path. For large existing text files, diff excerpts preserve original line numbers and indicate omissions; full-file versions detect subsequent changes.

conditions: Complete snapshot export is explicit.
exceptions: Assembly does not replace the accepted graph.
decisions.reason: Makes graph projection reproducible and protects readers from invalid candidate data.
decisions.text: Assembly is deterministic and model-free. By default it returns a bounded summary; explicit export provides the complete candidate snapshot for inspection or later admission, without replacing the accepted graph. Candidate snapshots have a versioned format and integrity hash; altered, unsupported, or incomplete data is rejected before being presented as graph content.

decisions.reason: Defines supported documentation scope and source selection.
decisions.text: Documentation may be uncommitted, need not be in a Git repository, and may use project-specific Markdown organization at monorepo, package, or module scope. Optional hivex.json configuration selects relative include, exclude, and archive globs. Without configuration, Hivex selects project Markdown while skipping dependencies, its cache, Git metadata, and private dot directories; explicitly named documentation directories can be selected.

conditions: A fourth revision requires explicit authorization; all per-round and lifetime invocation limits apply.
exceptions: Failed or unchanged replacement output remains failed; unchanged candidates are not sent through another fidelity review.
decisions.reason: Bounds revision work and preserves its complete evidence and consumption history.
decisions.text: Revise only the selected source in the existing cohort, preserving its earlier candidate, original result hash, full negative review, request, and attempt reports. Each revision round allows at most three attempts; three revisions are the default, with a fourth allowed only when explicitly authorized using a value from 1 to 4. A source has an absolute lifetime cap of twelve extraction invocations in the cohort, unaffected by failures or restarts. Check and clamp the global budget before claiming so exhaustion cannot leave a running claim or cause attempt thirteen. Existing size and reservation limits also apply. Failed or unchanged replacement output leaves an explicit failed source; unchanged output is not reviewed again. Safe retries preserve revision request, origin, and prior consumption; copied review usage remains in its original receipt and is not counted as an extraction call.

conditions: The skill reflects the actual CLI and workflow.
decisions.reason: Makes practical portable guidance part of delivery without overstating implementation completeness.
decisions.text: Each functional delivery includes a portable skill that teaches the actual CLI, agreed workflow, documentation practice, and cost and uncertainty handling without relying on private tools or unrelated skills. Named delivery slices are implementation stages, not proof that the complete contract has shipped.

conditions: Applies when changes affect project intent, constraints, decisions, or reasons.
decisions.reason: Keeps durable rationale available alongside executable behavior.
decisions.text: Code and executable contracts explain mechanics; Markdown preserves intent, constraints, decisions, and reasons. Update that knowledge alongside changes rather than leaving its only explanation in a conversation or private agent memory.

conditions: Applies to Rust control flow, including written macro tokens for the chain check.
exceptions: An ordinary `else` remains suitable for clear two-way value selection; `redundant_else` alone does not enforce the full preference.
decisions.reason: Encourages direct control flow without replacing clear decisions with abstractions.
decisions.text: Prefer early returns, `?`, `let-else`, and meaningful `match` expressions; do not use `else if` chains. The syntax gate checks expressions and written macro tokens while ignoring comments and string literals. Avoid artificial dispatch abstractions in place of clear decisions.

conditions: Complete current documents in the affected scope and complete prior closure evidence must be supplied.
exceptions: An update may finish with a warning pending when evidence is missing.
decisions.reason: Requires complete evidence for automatic warning disposition while keeping checks bounded.
decisions.text: The normal bounded check may dismiss descriptive observations or revalidate expired closures only for untargeted, non-validation cases when all in-scope current documents and the closure's complete prior evidence are in context. Missing evidence leaves the warning pending; findings or local validation failures prevent closure. Matching text alone is insufficient.

conditions: A fresh clone reuses only matching ingestion units.
Import requires no unfinished local work.
exceptions: An existing local graph remains in use until a snapshot is imported.
decisions.reason: Enables snapshot reuse without implicitly replacing local knowledge or accounting.
decisions.text: A fresh clone can query a shared snapshot without a local database; its first update reuses matching ingestion units and starts local work accounting. If a local graph already exists, it takes precedence until a snapshot is imported. Import refuses unfinished local work and does not reset attempts or budgets.

conditions: Compatibility covers the original Markdown, source identity, authority, section and line information, claims, relationships and their order, and review instructions.
exceptions: A matching document hash alone is insufficient; an incompatible contract blocks reuse.
decisions.reason: Preserved original evidence and verdict while allowing only fully compatible reassociation.
decisions.text: The former workflow reused a review across graph snapshots only when its complete source-review request was identical apart from the graph-hash marker and the model, native policy, and schema remained compatible. Preserve the original review, identities, verdict, invocation report, and usage; bind the new association to the original result and revalidate the association and original semantic inputs on subsequent reads and admission. Reuse makes no model call and cannot improve an adverse or insufficient assessment.

conditions: Integration must be owner-approved and the exact archive must already be published on npm.
decisions.reason: Makes GitHub release publication depend on approved integration and the exact npm artifact.
decisions.text: Only after owner approval of integration and publication of the exact archive on npm, create a new version tag on the reviewed release revision and publish its GitHub release. Never move an existing release tag; link the notes to the exact npm version and record the archive hash.

conditions: The principal reviewer remains responsible for accepting the implementation.
exceptions: Hivex does not conduct every aspect of code review or rewrite Markdown itself.
decisions.reason: Defines assistance and review responsibilities without delegating human acceptance or documentary authority.
decisions.text: Implementers consult Hivex before coherent feature or behavior changes; the principal reviewer consults it with the task and diff, checks its findings, and retains acceptance responsibility. Demonstrated contradictions require correction or an approved decision change; genuine unanswered decisions go to the owner with sources, impact, and a recommendation.

decisions.reason: Separates execution contracts from vendors and defines what invocation accounting covers.
decisions.text: An execution integration connects Hivex to an agent or runtime for bounded invocations and observes results, usage, cancellation, and cleanup; Codex is supported but is not a domain requirement. An execution profile includes the requested integration, provider, model, and result-affecting options, and must match effective execution; similarly named effort levels are not assumed equivalent. An attempt is an accounted invocation, including failures and unknown usage, and is retained when work resumes.

conditions: Use TDD only as an option for critical flows with sufficiently defined behavior.
Test a visual dimension when it is an intentional requirement worth maintaining.
exceptions: Do not require a test for every function, component, wrapper, or line.
decisions.reason: Prioritizes durable behavioral coverage over incidental implementation details.
decisions.text: Select tests for value and risk, emphasizing critical flows, stable rules, and demonstrated regressions. TDD is optional and suited to critical flows whose behavior is defined; explore unresolved behavior before encoding assumptions in tests. Tests need to protect supported behavior, meaningful invariants, or regressions, and should favor observable caller-facing results that survive refactors. For UI, cover visible content, accessibility, interactions, and loading, error, and empty states. Test visual dimensions only when they are intentional requirements, not incidental structure or styling.

conditions: Historical sources enter consultation through focused selection or a known dependency.
decisions.reason: Separates availability of historical evidence from ordinary ingestion and current applicability.
decisions.text: Archived Markdown remains readable evidence but is outside ordinary update and consultation ingestion. A focused source selection or known relationship may supply bounded ranges. Historical metadata and evidence keep extracted decisions historical even if transport suggests another status.

conditions: Applies to changes in rules, parser versions, or the dependency matrix.
decisions.reason: Keeps the policy and its representative tests aligned with changes.
decisions.text: When rules, parser versions, or the dependency matrix change, update this authority and representative positive and negative cases.

conditions: When decision text is moved or an ADR is superseded.
decisions.reason: Compacts current documentation without losing provenance or applicable constraints.
decisions.text: Authors may move replaced decision text into clearly historical Markdown while preserving its text, dates, and provenance. The current ADR keeps applicable decisions, reasons, dependencies, and exceptions, with links to history and replacements. A fully superseded ADR may remain as a pointer at its original path; preserve referenced anchors or update callers, and do not treat age alone as making an applicable condition obsolete.

conditions: The effective profile is recorded when it is known.
decisions.reason: Preserves provenance for the requested and observed execution profiles without assuming an unknown effective profile.
decisions.text: Each new work item records its requested profile, and an execution receipt records the observed effective profile when known.

conditions: Retained relationships require supplied endpoints and complete current citations.
exceptions: Removed interpretations alone are not treated as current defects.
decisions.reason: Keeps findings scoped to the materialized candidate and prevents reuse of stale assessments.
decisions.text: Materialized checks separate candidate knowledge from interpretations being replaced. Prior decisions are comparison evidence with candidate existence indicated. Checks include retained same-work relationships only between supplied endpoints with current, fully supplied citations; unrelated edges are not copied into every check. Removed interpretations alone are not current defects, but missing replacements and faulty retained endpoints remain findings. Changed check requests cannot reuse an old receipt.

conditions: Pointers should identify relevant authority for the task.
exceptions: No required fields or line-count threshold applies.
decisions.reason: Makes the entrypoint selective and useful without adding a new format gate.
decisions.text: Keep AGENTS.md brief: provide orientation, knowledge pointers, development/verification guidance, and only needed project constraints. Point to relevant authority with enough context, avoid duplicating other documents, and do not require every document on every task. The convention is ordinary Markdown without required fields; the foundation is not a schema or line-count gate.

decisions.reason: Keeps area classification project-specific and useful.
decisions.text: Use area or component labels that fit this project, preserve useful existing classification, and avoid importing another product's area catalogue or duplicating the issue title.

conditions: IDs, schema membership, counts, evidence, and retained bindings must validate under the applicable contract.
exceptions: A source may override the global fallback schema hash.
decisions.reason: Keeps model output bounded and its evidence and contract verifiable.
decisions.text: Use the compact review contract with source-local claim and relationship IDs, exact schema membership and counts, and literal evidence with exact newlines and no normalization. Expand retained results back to graph identities and validate review bindings and output hash. The global schema hash is the fallback unless a source specifies an effective override; a different contract blocks reuse and retention validation, with no compatibility adapter or receipt relabelling.

decisions.reason: Records current domain boundaries and integration ownership.
decisions.text: Current module ownership assigns source handling and parsing to src/documents; graph and derived state to src/knowledge; typed progress, budgets, and persistence to src/work; and composition to consultation and review. The execution contract is integration-neutral, Codex protocol and lifecycle code belongs under src/integrations/codex, and CLI and development tools remain separate.

conditions: A changed request or divergent graph prevents reuse of the retained check.
With no available call, a changed candidate remains pending.
exceptions: This process does not reassess an adverse model check as if it were a local defect.
decisions.reason: Permits local admission fixes without erasing the original assessment or budget history.
decisions.text: A local admission defect may be reassessed against a retained check without another model call, preserving the original failed assessment and consumption. The reassessment must match the exact candidate and request, current evidence, and graph state; it does not rerun an adverse model check. Older unfinished work keeps its original request and budget. When a repair references a current supplied decision, that decision is retained as check context; an older candidate that discarded such an endpoint may reuse its extraction for a check of the corrected candidate within the same allowance.

conditions: Replacement is owner-authorized.
exceptions: Historical evidence remains unchanged.
decisions.reason: Allows the approved workflow replacement while preserving the prior evidence as history.
decisions.text: The owner-authorized implementation can replace the earlier cohort/admission pipeline; historical evidence remains unchanged.

conditions: Applies when following the npm onboarding path.
decisions.reason: Keeps the installed CLI dependency local to and pinned for the project.
decisions.text: The npm onboarding path installs Hivex as an exact, project-local development dependency before initialization.

decisions.reason: Defines Rust domain boundaries while allowing the concrete collaborations the project needs.
decisions.text: Knowledge, work, and execution accounting may collaborate without imposing an acyclic layering. Execution validates knowledge output and persists work evidence; integrations remain vendor-neutral at the contract level, isolated by vendor, and cannot import knowledge, work, or CLI. Integration, provider, model, and options are independent choices.

decisions.reason: Makes original code citation ranges recoverable without changing the source blob.
decisions.text: Represent each code version in model requests as one-based numbered original lines, retaining exact text, empty lines and CRLF carriage returns so LF-joining reconstructs the blob. This replaces unnumbered prompt text and changes the prompt hash, not code, manifests or citation validation.

conditions: The assessment concerns the supplied source and complete set of claims and relationships.
exceptions: A represented prerequisite or link does not by itself require reviewing the referenced document.
decisions.reason: Literal provenance establishes citation, not preservation of the source's meaning.
decisions.text: Assess substantive assertions rather than duplicating provenance labels or examples unless they add a distinct rule, reason, exception, or behavior. Check every supplied claim and relationship once against the source, including omissions, negation, conditions, exceptions, scope, proposal status, order, and context sufficiency. Judge references to other documents for faithful representation; a reference alone does not require its target, but missing context that prevents assessing fidelity leaves the review unresolved.

decisions.reason: Preserves documentary authority and source provenance.
decisions.text: Hivex does not compact, move, or rewrite Markdown. Authors preserve historical text, dates, links, and anchors; Hivex exposes selected source versions and line ranges while retaining historical applicability and conditions.

conditions: Local verification is required when CI is unavailable.
decisions.reason: Preserves the approved CI execution and untrusted-code boundary.
decisions.text: Quality CI runs on an ephemeral GitHub-hosted macOS 15 ARM64 runner and checks the environment and architecture before native gates. PRs receive read-only repository permissions and no stored credentials or publishing secrets. Do not reconnect a personal workstation or use pull_request_target to check out untrusted code. Queued, skipped, or interrupted CI is not a pass; require local verification when CI is unavailable.

conditions: Applies when using those ADRs as evidence.
decisions.reason: Prevents historical workflow descriptions from being mistaken for current acceptance.
decisions.text: Treat ADRs 0004–0009 as historical accounts of the replaced experimental cohort/admission workflow, not current acceptance evidence. The map identifies ADR 0010 as superseding the mandatory ceremony; historical evidence remains scoped to its original revision.

conditions: Retire obsolete machinery only after knowledge recovery and replacement validation.
exceptions: The replacement workflow may be used before all historical artifacts are retired if remaining work is explicit.
decisions.reason: Allows a staged replacement without losing historical evidence or retaining obsolete active systems indefinitely.
decisions.text: After knowledge recovery and replacement validation, remove obsolete active machinery while preserving useful decisions in canonical documents and necessary historical evidence in Git or a bounded private archive. Do not rewrite Git history or destroy the accepted Opus graph before its replacement is admitted. A replacement may be used while explicitly identified retirement work remains; closure requires useful historical knowledge in Markdown and obsolete active machinery retired where no longer needed. Validate against bounded real cases, not identity with the old graph or exhaustive replay.

decisions.reason: Separates version currency from whether a decision applies.
decisions.text: Applicability asks whether a decision governs a case after its conditions, exceptions, and replacements are considered. Freshness asks whether derived knowledge still matches selected source versions; freshness alone establishes neither applicability nor correctness.

decisions.reason: The source explicitly records this as the original choice and identifies its later replacement.
decisions.text: The original knowledge-model default was gpt-5.6-luna at maximum effort.

conditions: When historical evidence is needed, retrieve it within the declared scope.
decisions.reason: Preserves historical evidence without confusing it with current rules or silently losing dependencies.
decisions.text: Historical sources remain available for bounded retrieval when needed, but do not enter ordinary ingestion or consultation merely because they are accessible. Hivex must honor the declared source scope and report necessary evidence that is unavailable rather than silently omitting a dependency or treating an old rule as current. Authors, not Hivex, perform documentary compaction.

conditions: The TypeScript documentation template applies only when relevant to an adopting TypeScript project.
decisions.reason: Separates Hivex's Rust standards from optional adopter guidance while preserving human-maintained Markdown authority.
decisions.text: The approved Rust quality standard replaces the earlier objection to Rust thresholds, using maintained tools and explicit project preferences without claiming equivalence to ESLint or the TypeScript template. The optional TypeScript documentation template applies to adopting TypeScript projects, not Hivex development. Repository Markdown remains human-maintained authority; check changed links, commands, and scope without retaining a JavaScript formatter solely for documentation.

conditions: All required current documents and prior closure evidence must be in context.
exceptions: Findings and local validation failures cannot use the automatic closure path.
decisions.reason: Prevents warning dismissal or revalidation from relying on incomplete or text-only evidence.
decisions.text: A new work item uses its normal bounded check to inspect new uncertainties and revalidate expired closures affected by changed sources. Automatic dismissal or revalidation is limited to descriptive observations and untargeted, non-validation closures, and requires complete current in-scope documents plus complete prior closure evidence. Findings and local validation failures are excluded; missing evidence leaves warnings pending. Matching text alone is insufficient.

conditions: Applies when nested active patterns conflict with root ignore behavior.
decisions.reason: Prevents proceeding with conflicting local-state or snapshot visibility.
decisions.text: If active patterns in a nested .hivex/.gitignore can expose local state or hide the snapshot, initialization reports the conflict before writing files; reconcile those patterns with the root ignore policy before continuing.

conditions: The transition applies only to unfinished work under the former GPT-5.6 Luna/max default.
exceptions: Running or uncertain invocations require normal inspection and recovery.
Failed work still requires explicit retry.
decisions.reason: Updates resumable work while preserving its identity, accounting, and historical results.
decisions.text: Unfinished work under the former GPT-5.6 Luna/max default profile moves to the current GPT-6 Luna profile when resumed, preserving its work ID, progress, attempts, and consumption. Completed work and answers remain historical rather than being reused as results under the new profile. Running or uncertain work requires normal inspection and recovery, and failed work requires explicit retry. Changing the default alone does not reingest graph knowledge; other profile changes block unfinished work with EXECUTION_PROFILE_CHANGED without making a model call or resetting consumption.

decisions.reason: Retained as past state only: the supplied guide describes the current CLI as native Rust, and ADR 0003 says its Bun runtime and development requirements were superseded.
decisions.text: The original product stack was TypeScript and Bun.

decisions.reason: Keeps labels semantically distinct and prevents them from being mistaken for model or authorization controls.
decisions.text: Use readiness, participation, dependency, type, scope, and risk labels for their distinct purposes. Labels do not select models or grant permission. Work labels should survive skill replacement, and aliases that duplicate existing meaning should be avoided.

conditions: The prior invocation must have ended safely, and the retry must fit within the round's total attempt budget.
exceptions: Unconfirmed starts or interruptions, failed cleanup, successful candidates, and unresolved claims cannot be retried through this operation.
decisions.reason: Allows bounded recovery without mistaking uncertain execution for a safe retry.
decisions.text: Retry a retained failed source only through an explicit operation and only after a safely ended failure: failed admission without an accepted turn, invalid output after confirmed completion and cleanup, or acknowledged interruption with confirmed cleanup. Preserve earlier reports and consumption; the attempt limit is a total of at most three for the extraction round, including prior calls. Claim the source and reserve result capacity before retrying against its original frozen source. Only invalid extraction receives correction feedback. Ordinary ingestion never implicitly retries failures.

conditions: Every relationship retained its evidence, endpoint assessments, conditions, exceptions, and affected scope.
exceptions: A represented external reference or an unrelated claim did not by itself require its external document or prototype; missing context still blocked assessment when needed to judge fidelity or a relationship within the selected pair.
decisions.reason: Kept pair findings evidence-bound and scoped, and distinguished authored resolution from unresolved conflict.
decisions.text: The former comparison contract assessed every supplied claim once. Relationships connected claims from different sources, cited both endpoints, and were referenced by both endpoint assessments; conditions, exceptions, and affected scope remained explicit. Source-qualified model IDs were bound to graph identities, while hashes preserved normalized and expanded output. Success depended on the complete validated assessment, not a global verdict: reported contradictions, unknown scope, incomplete coverage, unresolved claims, or insufficient context prevented success, while valid negative findings remained available. Dates, status labels, and identifier order alone did not establish precedence. An authored amendment required evidence and a scoped supersession or exception; contradiction was reserved for unresolved incompatibility. Clarifications changed the request contract without relabelling prior results, and invalid output remained untrusted diagnostics rather than a partial assessment. Pair comparisons did not establish doctrine or admission.

conditions: Supporting-source context is subject to the same context limit.
decisions.reason: Keeps repair source-bound and prevents its reason or context from becoming policy.
decisions.text: A repair reason guides comparison with Markdown but is not authority, and repair does not edit the source. An explicitly selected supporting source contributes its complete Markdown and current decisions as context, not as an ingestion target. Its selection and versions identify the work; genuine documentary conflict still requires the responsible person’s decision.

conditions: The project syntax gate enforces this function-local definition.
exceptions: The function or closure body itself is excluded from the count.
decisions.reason: Defines nesting locally so container depth and closure syntax do not distort the project limit.
decisions.text: Allow at most three nested blocks inside a function or block-bodied closure, excluding its body block. Each function or closure has its own count; explicit inner scopes count, while enclosing `impl`, trait, and inline-module containers do not. The syntax gate applies an implicit body boundary to expression-bodied closures.

decisions.reason: Establishes versioned source retrieval as the initial product capability and preserves source authority.
decisions.text: Hivex begins with search over versioned sources and expansion, with authored documentation and accepted history retaining authority over generated knowledge.

conditions: Applies to persistent state, temporary resources, and generated diagnostics.
exceptions: A database transaction may serve as an atomic checkpoint without a separate file; diagnostics may be exported when needed rather than written for each successful step.
decisions.reason: Controls data growth and artifacts while preserving recoverability and evidence.
decisions.text: Define the purpose, location, owner, and retention before adding persistent state. Bound cached data, run history, and diagnostics. Read-only queries should leave no per-query artifacts; clean up owned temporary resources on ordinary completion and handled failures. Interrupted work must remain recoverable without silent retry or discard. Retention must preserve accepted state and evidence needed by supported recovery or historical operations.

conditions: The complete snapshot must fit the 256 MiB artifact and requested-output limits; the embedded candidate and assessments retain their 64 MiB and 8 MiB limits.
A limit failure never returns a partial accepted artifact.
exceptions: Hivex does not create separate files per claim, comparison, admission attempt or query.
decisions.reason: Makes the full, reproducible artifact caller-owned instead of creating persistent per-operation files.
decisions.text: Admission is deterministic and makes no model calls. Export one complete artifact on request; routine checking and querying create no files. The caller retains the artifact and commits it with the knowledge configuration. JSON round-trips must preserve admission and hashes without model work.

conditions: Reuse knowledge only when structural and source-version checks match.
Update changed sources as necessary.
exceptions: Partial or uncertain coverage may remain explicit in a snapshot.
decisions.reason: Supports incremental reuse while making freshness and operation effects visible.
decisions.text: Use deterministic structural and source-version checks to identify reusable, stale, or unavailable knowledge. A fresh clone should reuse matching knowledge; changed sources require only the necessary update. Snapshots may retain explicit partial or uncertain coverage, serialization of the same graph should have a stable diff, and read-only queries should not dirty the shared file. Snapshot operations must not trigger hidden model calls or source edits.

exceptions: Use model assistance when it adds useful interpretation.
decisions.reason: Keeps warning review grounded and avoids compelled retries or automated repairs.
decisions.text: Warning review adds no mandatory model call, retry, or automatic semantic repair. Use deterministic local retrieval and source inspection first; invoke Luna/max only when it adds useful interpretation.

conditions: Applicability claims must be supported by source evidence.
exceptions: The recommended Markdown convention is not mandatory.
decisions.reason: Keeps project knowledge grounded in its sources without limiting projects to one documentation format.
decisions.text: Markdown is documentary authority and may follow each project's organization and format. Maintain a semantic graph of meaningful decisions and explicit or implicit relationships, retrieve relevant transitive dependencies within a context budget, and explain applicability only when evidence supports it. The recommended Markdown convention is guidance, not an admission requirement.

conditions: Run the development-guide checks before archive preparation.
exceptions: A different archive path may be supplied for a new verification build.
decisions.reason: Defines controlled archive preparation without publication or overwriting prior artifacts.
decisions.text: Keep Cargo and npm package versions aligned, run the development-guide checks, then prepare the native archive with the locked release-target pack command. Preparation stages the public allowlist and metadata, writes an npm-compatible tarball and JSON report, and does not publish or run a package manager. Existing archives are not overwritten; use a different explicit path for another verification build.

conditions: Before publication of each package artifact.
exceptions: A repacked artifact is acceptable only after a fresh inspection and scan.
decisions.reason: Binds the security check to the exact artifact being published.
decisions.text: Before publication, inspect and scan the exact package archive for secrets and unintended private content, record its hash and scan result, and publish that same verified artifact. Repacking requires a fresh check; do not substitute an unchecked reconstruction from a changed working tree.

conditions: Git or tracker changes remain within the owner’s authorization.
decisions.reason: Keeps semantic migration and project-specific choices under responsible human control.
decisions.text: Migrate existing documentation when reasonably possible while preserving useful content, links, history, and scope. The CLI does not infer semantic migrations or overwrite sources. Git and tracker conventions are aligned only within owner authorization; project-specific areas remain local.

conditions: A missing status must be resolved from content rather than assumed accepted.
exceptions: Tags are optional; title and date can improve cataloguing.
decisions.reason: Keeps current applicability and replacement scope distinct from historical reasoning.
decisions.text: Use truthful status and, when useful, a title and decision date; tags are optional. When replacing a rule, identify the replacement and whether the change is partial. Preserve historical reasoning rather than silently rewriting it; a missing status is unresolved, not proof of acceptance.

conditions: The correction identifies the work and check and includes a source-backed reason and versioned evidence.
The check uses the original work budget; if no calls remain, the candidate stays pending.
The relationship-loss guard continues to apply, including to relationships removed from the accepted graph.
exceptions: A relationship-only correction may provide no decision replacements.
Corrections cannot be combined with candidate-finding resolution; replaying the same correction is idempotent.
decisions.reason: Keeps candidate changes reviewable, source-bound, and within the original work scope and budget.
decisions.text: A retained candidate can be corrected with source-backed, versioned evidence without repeating extraction, but a fresh check is still required. Decision replacements use existing local IDs and stay within the original document and pending ranges; adding decisions is unsupported. Relationship edits must touch a pending decision, cite supplied current evidence, and may point to a current supplied decision retained in the candidate. Invalid endpoints, out-of-scope or stale evidence, duplicate IDs, contradictory edits, dangling references, and corrections that leave the materialized result unchanged are rejected. Corrections and prior attempts remain recorded.

exceptions: A visible blocked marker is optional when it does not help selection.
decisions.reason: Separates dependency blockers and scheduling from defined scope.
decisions.text: Represent actual blockers with native issue dependencies and use a blocked marker when it aids selection. Deferred work is decided but intentionally unscheduled. Do not start blocked or deferred work merely because its scope is defined.

conditions: Grounding must use the reviewed code or diff revision and exact graph manifest.
Evidence must resolve applicable conditions, exceptions, and partial supersession.
Tests and code review remain necessary.
exceptions: Contradictions, insufficient evidence, execution failures, and incomplete retrieval bar automatic acceptance.
decisions.reason: Preserves the stated staged grounding requirement without implying that the initial extraction interface delivered it.
decisions.text: Implementation grounding binds review to the reviewed code or diff revision and exact graph manifest. Evidence must resolve applicable conditions, exceptions, and partial supersession; contradictions, insufficient evidence, execution failures, or incomplete retrieval cannot lead to automatic acceptance. Tests and code review remain necessary alongside grounding. This is a separate staged requirement not delivered by the initial extract interface.

conditions: Range repair requires current source coverage.
A reassessment without another model call requires candidate identity, evidence freshness, and graph continuity.
exceptions: Inherited neighbor uncertainty alone is not a new rejection finding.
decisions.reason: Localizes repair without losing supported relationships or laundering failed assessments.
decisions.text: Range repair expands selected sources to bounded ingestion units while preserving unaffected knowledge and requires current source coverage. New work uses its normal single check. Do not discard relationships supported by current evidence without source-grounded justification; otherwise retain the prior graph and attempt. Admission uses current-check findings rather than inherited neighbor uncertainty, but still rejects current findings affecting the relationship or endpoints and invalid evidence. Reassessment without another model call requires validated candidate identity, fresh evidence, and graph continuity, while preserving the original failure and budget.

conditions: The context decision concerned the supplied pair, not the external truth of a reference.
exceptions: External material need not be supplied solely to verify a reference's external basis.
decisions.reason: Kept context requirements proportional to the former pair assessment's scope.
decisions.text: Context sufficiency in the former comparison workflow was judged for the selected pair. A faithfully represented reference or a claim unrelated to the other source did not alone require supplying an external document or prototype. Missing context still blocked assessment when needed to judge candidate fidelity or an actual relationship within the pair.

conditions: Dependency checks apply to production modules and paths.
exceptions: Explicit test-only modules and functions are excluded from dependency checks, but not behavior or source-quality verification.
decisions.reason: States the architecture gate's enforcement boundary and its limits.
decisions.text: The architecture test follows production modules from the main entry point and checks imports, qualified paths, and private submodules. It rejects root aliases or glob imports and custom production path redirection. Test-only modules and functions are excluded from dependency checks, but their behavior and source quality remain subject to verification. The gate is not a compiler name-resolution engine or a security sandbox for arbitrary macro expansion.

conditions: Indirect traversal is bounded by the supplied limit.
decisions.reason: Bounds retrieval and distinguishes stale knowledge from current evidence.
decisions.text: Search and neighbor traversal are deterministic and make no model calls. Neighbor traversal includes indirect connections within its limit and lists decisions it could not expand. Stale knowledge is not current evidence, and status reports available knowledge and documents needing attention.

conditions: The host must complete the stated verification before supplying source text.
decisions.reason: Constrains execution admission and prevents silent changes to authority, configuration, or provider.
decisions.text: Before source is supplied, the host verifies the admitted CLI protocol, account type, first-party endpoint, effective model and effort, and unavailable model tools. It must not use private agent memory, project instructions discovered in a checkout, or provider fallback; its controls preserve the user’s configuration for other work. Codex remains the execution harness, not a session fleet.

conditions: Each precedence assessment cites every distinct endpoint source, including for inapplicable relations.
exceptions: Structural validation supports semantic assessment but does not prove the model interpreted a valid quotation correctly.
decisions.reason: Makes verdicts depend on complete, scoped and verifiable evidence rather than unexamined precedence claims.
decisions.text: Assess every supplied changed/context file and source once for relevance and coverage. Give supersessions and exceptions explicit dispositions and affected scope, preserving conditions, negations and partial scope; cite both endpoint sources and implementation when resolving a relation. Validate original citation ranges/text, coverage identities and supplied precedence relations. A definitive verdict requires relevant cited changed code and documentation, complete coverage, sufficient context and no unresolved applicability.

conditions: Bundled skills and CLI must use the same release.
exceptions: Existing skill directories and links are preserved.
decisions.reason: Keeps bundled skills consistent and prevents initialization from following unsafe parent links.
decisions.text: The package includes the CLI and six bundled skills. Install the skill directories together at the CLI’s release and preserve their relative references. Initialization links them into agent skill locations, preserves existing skill directories or links, and rejects parent-directory symlinks before writing.

conditions: Review new active and reopened entries against current sources.
decisions.reason: Makes warning changes interpretable across resumptions and source transitions without implying full-backlog review.
decisions.text: For new update work, warningChanges compares warning IDs and closure status with the work-start baseline, which persists through resumption and is independent of source-coverage freshness. New IDs were absent at the start; resolved IDs had no closure at the start and end with one; reopened IDs had earlier closures whose evidence became stale before or during the work and remain reopened until revalidated. A current-source closure can predate ingestion. The report describes that work, not the complete warning backlog.

decisions.reason: Sets product and documentation ownership boundaries.
decisions.text: Projects use a small versioned source configuration. Hivex does not create private agent memory, a hosted documentation database, or another session orchestrator; Hivex documentation stays in its repository and project-specific language and decisions stay in the project’s documentation.

conditions: The directory distinction is an adoption default.
exceptions: An existing arrangement may remain where migration would not be appropriate.
decisions.reason: Keeps document collections understandable without forcing needless restructuring.
decisions.text: Use guidelines for standing rules and design guidance, and procedures for carrying out tasks; avoid overlapping directories with indistinct purposes. These organization choices are defaults, not a reason to migrate an existing arrangement when migration is inappropriate.

conditions: Migration is preferred when reasonably possible.
exceptions: An existing layout may remain; organization is not required for ingestion.
decisions.reason: Encourages useful organization without making migration a condition of use.
decisions.text: For adoption, prefer migration to the recommended structure when reasonably possible while preserving useful documents, authority, history, and links. Other Markdown layouts remain readable and are not an ingestion prerequisite.

decisions.reason: Makes execution limits and consumption visible instead of silently weakening evidence review.
decisions.text: Native operations accept integration, model, effort, provider, Codex, and deadline options; the default deadline is 30 minutes. Consultation context defaults to 65,536 bytes and can be bounded. Limits must be reported rather than met by silently cutting rules or implying omitted evidence was reviewed. Call and input-byte budgets limit work, while reported token usage reflects known actual consumption, including failed attempts.

decisions.reason: Protects revision consistency and prevents incomplete evidence from being presented as complete.
decisions.text: Search and read must refer to the same immutable revision. The index is disposable derived data, initially built in memory for each search.
